D. Phase II - Metallic Surfaces and Structures Inspection
SUBTASK 05-51-19-210-030
NOTE: If a 50 flight cycle deferral is provided, perform these steps on or before the 50 flight cycle
limit.
(1) Perform a General Visual Inspection (GVI) of Zones 1, 2 and 3 metallic surface areas for signs
of lightning strike damage (Figure 202).
(a) Utilize any available equipment at the time to examine required areas of the aircraft.
(b) Zone 1 includes these areas:
1) Wing Leading Edge (LE)
2) Wing Trailing Edge (TE)
3) Wingtips/Winglets
4) Engines
5) Vertical Fin Tip
6) Horizontal Stabilizer Tips
7) Elevators
8) Nose Radome
9) Tailcone Area.
(c) Examine the fuel areas of the wing torque box (Figure 201).
NOTE: A wing torque box includes the outboard wing, the wing center section, and the
side of the body structure. The outboard wing has upper and lower skin panels
and front and rear spar with ribs found perpendicular to the rear spar. The center
section contains an in-spar wing box and a wing-to-body interface structure.
(d) Examine all external metallic surfaces for any evidence of visible external lightning strike
damage.
(e) Examine the external metallic surfaces to find the lightning strike attach points.
(f) Look in the areas where one surface stops and another surface starts (for example, butt
joints and lap joints).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(g) Examine the metallic structure looking for signs of lightning strike damage such as: holes,
pits, melting, burns or discoloration.
CAUTION
SEAL OR REPAIR ALL DAMAGE. IF YOU DO NOT SEAL OR REPAIR ALL
DAMAGE, MOISTURE CAN GET IN. MOISTURE CAN CAUSE MORE
INTERNAL DAMAGE.
(h) Repair or seal the damaged areas per the Structural Repair Manual (SRM).
E. Phase II - Composite Surfaces and Structures Inspection
SUBTASK 05-51-19-210-031
NOTE: If a 50 flight cycle deferral is provided, perform these steps on or before the 50 flight cycle
limit.
(1) Perform a GVI of Zones 1, 2 and 3 composite surface areas for signs of lightning strike
damage (Figure 202).
(a) Utilize any available equipment at the time to examine required areas of the aircraft.
(b) Zone 1 includes these areas:
1) Wing LE
2) Wing TE
3) Wingtips/Winglets
4) Engines
5) Vertical Fin Tip
6) Horizontal Stabilizer Tips
7) Elevators
8) Nose Radome
9) Tailcone Area.
(c) Examine all composite structures for discolored paint, burned, or punctured skin.
(d) Examine the external composite surfaces to find the lightning strike attach points.
(e) Look in the areas where one surface stops and another surface starts (for example, butt
joints and lap joints).
(f) Examine the external composite surfaces of the nose radome for burns, punctures, and
pin holes in the composite honeycomb sandwich structure.
1) If damage is found, examine the internal surfaces and components under the nose
radome.
(g) Examine the external composite surfaces for discolored paint, burns or punctures.
1) If lightning strike damage is found, examine all composite structure in perimeter of
damaged area for signs of delamination.
NOTE: Types of damage you cannot see, like delamination, can extend to the
areas beyond the lightning strike damage. You can find delamination by
instrumental Non-Destructive Inspection (NDI) methods or by a tap test.
2) Use instrumental or non-instrumental NDI tap testing to find composite structure
delamination you cannot see.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
a) For a tap test, use a solid metal disk and tap the area adjacent to the
damaged area lightly.
NOTE: If there is delamination, you will hear a sound that is different than the
sound of a solid bonded area. Refer to the Nondestructive Test
Manual.
CAUTION
SEAL OR REPAIR ALL DAMAGE. IF YOU DO NOT SEAL OR REPAIR ALL
DAMAGE, MOISTURE CAN GET IN. MOISTURE CAN CAUSE MORE
INTERNAL DAMAGE.
(h) Repair or seal the damaged areas per the SRM.
SUBTASK 05-51-19-210-035
(2) Perform a GVI of the wingtips or winglets composite structure.
(a) If the composite structure show signs of lightning strike damage, address the damage per
the SRM or approved method.
F. Phase II - System Components Inspection
SUBTASK 05-51-19-210-052
(1) Perform a detailed inspection of the Angle of Attack (AOA) sensors.
(a) Do a movement check of the AOA sensors.
NOTE: The movement must be smooth and must not have any rough spots in the travel
range during the movement check.
(b) Examine for melted sealant or damaged AOA sensors.
SUBTASK 05-51-19-210-053
(2) Examine the pitot probes, static ports, and the areas around them for damage and look for
burns, punctures, discolored paint, and general skin distortion.
(a) If damage is found, the damage must be assessed and/or repaired per the SRM or
approved method.
SUBTASK 05-51-19-210-033
(3) Perform a GVI of all of the external lights.
(a) Look for these items:
1) Broken light assemblies.
2) Broken or cracked lenses.
3) Other visible damage.
(b) If you find damaged lights, do these steps:
1) Examine these items:
a) The internal wires of the light fixture for damage.
b) The first 3 ft (1 m) of wiring from the damaged light in the direction of the
circuit breaker.
c) The circuit breaker terminals and the first 1 in. (25 mm) of wires from the
terminals.
2) Repair or replace damaged parts as necessary until the light functions properly.
3) If the circuit breaker did not trip, then no further examinations for the wiring of the
damaged light are required.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
4) If the circuit breaker did trip, then locate the source of the anomaly and repair as
necessary.
(c) Do a test of the lights that follow:
1) Do this task: Anti-Collision Lights - Operational Test, TASK 33-44-00-710-801.
2) Do this task: Emergency Lights - Operational Check, TASK 33-51-00-710-801.

(b) Make sure that there is full travel and the flight controls move freely.

05-51-21-210-801Filiform Corrosion - (Conditional Inspection)PDF p. 973
2. Filiform Corrosion - (Conditional Inspection)
A. General
(1) The standard for the inspection is a General Visual Inspection.
NOTE: The Limited Return to Service Plan (LRTS) is only applicable to filiform corrosion.
(2) If FC is found, do a Limited Inspection in 30 days.
(a) The Limited Inspection is specified to areas prone to FC (Figure 201). These areas
include:
• Butt joints
• Lap splices
• Cutouts
• Areas on and around fasteners common to the skin panels and lap splices
• Access doors
(b) All inspection areas are below the lower lap splice of the window belt at stringer S-14.
(3) Mild to moderate filiform corrosion (FC) that does not advance to severe must be removed
within 3 years.
(4) The LRTS plan can be used if mild to moderate FC is found. All severe FC must be removed
within 30 days with glass-bead blasting per SRM 51-10-02 or CORROSION REMOVAL,
SUBJECT 51-00-53.
(a) The LRTS plan has repeated inspections and surveys.
1) The repeat inspections are mandatory every 120 days after the discovery of the FC.
2) The LRTS plan is not applicable if all known areas of FC are removed from the
aircraft. Subject aircraft can return to service.
B. References
Reference Title
51-00-53 CORROSION REMOVAL
SRM 51-10-02 Structural Repair Manual
C. Tools/Equipment
Reference Description
STD-4055 6 Inch Minimum Length Stainless Steel Pocket Ruler, 1/32" And
1/64" Increments, or Mm And Cm Increments
STD-6732 Camera - 35mm, Single Lens Reflex Type
STD-14360 Flashlight
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
D. Location Zones
Zone Area
100 Lower Half of Fuselage
E. Limited Inspection Procedure
SUBTASK 05-51-21-210-001
(1) Put the aircraft in an area that is free from rain and other conditions that can affect a visual
inspection.
NOTE: Rain and moisture can prevent correct identification of FC. The inspection location
must be dry.
SUBTASK 05-51-21-210-002
(2) Document each location of FC with a minimum of three pictures with a camera, STD-6732.
(a) A wide view picture to show the general location on the aircraft.
1) Include a monument in the picture. This will help to find the general area of the FC.
(b) A nearer picture, in the limits of the first picture, to show the location of the FC.
(c) A close-up picture of the FC.
1) Use a pocket ruler, STD-4055 to show the initial area dimension of the FC.
2) Identify the stations and stringer locations surrounding the FC.
3) A flashlight, STD-14360 can be used to help identify FC.
a) The flashlight angle can be varied to help maximize the contrast of the FC.
Use a direction which shows the FC clearly.
NOTE: A recommended angle is 15 degrees or less.
(3) Compare the FC found with the images in Figure 202 and Figure 203.
(a) For mild to moderate FC, use one of the two options:
1) Option 1:
a) Utilize the LRTS plan, reference Figure 204.
2) Option 2:
a) Remove all found instances of FC with glass-bead blasting. Refer to SRM
51-10-02 or CORROSION REMOVAL, SUBJECT 51-00-53. LRTS plan is not
applicable and the aircraft can return to service.
(b) For severe FC:
1) Severe FC must be removed from the aircraft within 30 days of initial discovery with
glass-bead blasting. Refer to SRM 51-10-02 or CORROSION REMOVAL,
SUBJECT 51-00-53.
NOTE: The LRTS plan is not applicable to severe FC.
(c) If mild to moderate and severe FC is found, do one of the two options:
1) Option 1:
a) Utilize the LRTS plan for the mild to moderate FC.
b) Severe FC must be removed from the aircraft within 30 days of initial
discovery with glass-bead blasting. Refer to SRM 51-10-02 or CORROSION
REMOVAL, SUBJECT 51-00-53.
NOTE: The LRTS plan is not applicable to severe FC.
2) Option 2:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
a) Remove all instances of FC from the aircraft with glass-bead blasting. Refer
toSRM 51-10-02 or CORROSION REMOVAL, SUBJECT 51-00-53. The LRTS
plan is not applicable and the aircraft can return to service.

D. Examine the Titanium Parts
NOTE: Titanium parts found in hydraulic fluid areas have a flat, black inorganic finish, or a gold coat
for protection.
NOTE: Make sure that the black finish is not hydraulic fluid.
SUBTASK 05-51-22-210-001
(1) Examine all of the titanium parts in these areas for contamination, and metal or paint
deterioration:
NOTE: Look for contamination, metal deterioration, or paint deterioration.
(a) High temperature ducts:
1) the ducts in the wheel well areas
2) the engine fan case
3) the engine fire walls
4) the ducts in the aft fuselage between the pressure bulkhead and the APU firewall
5) the pneumatic ducting along the leading edge of the wing
(b) Other Titanium Parts:
1) engine strut torque box interior structure
NOTE: Engine strut torque box interior structure have a high temperature coating
that is olive or beige color depending on age.
2) the landing gear beam
3) the APU support structure
4) the stabilizer links
E. Cleaning Contaminated Titanium Parts
SUBTASK 05-51-22-110-001
(1) To clean the titanium parts that were contaminated with low-temperature hydraulic fluid, do the
following:
NOTE: When hydraulic fluid leaks onto a High Temperature Duct, the hydraulic fluid should be
considered high temperature.
(a) Clean the titanium with a manual cleaner such as the ones that follow, do this task:
Cleaners and Polishes, TASK 20-30-31-910-801
1) solvent, B00153.
2) Altrex B cleaner, B00230.
3) Honey Bee 60 cleaner, B00638.
4) solvent, B50085.
(b) Remove the hydraulic fluid residue with solvent, B50085, or solvent, B00062, and hard
resin phenolic scraper, STD-1064.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 05-51-22-100-001
(2) Clean and treat titanium parts that were contaminated with high-temperature hydraulic fluid, do
the steps that follow:
CAUTION
DO NOT USE A VAPOR DEGREASER OR METHYL ALCOHOL TO CLEAN
TITANIUM PARTS OR TITANIUM ALLOY PARTS. ALSO, DO NOT USE
CHLORINATED MANUAL SOLVENTS ON TITANIUM OR TITANIUM ALLOY
PARTS. DO NOT APPLY THESE MATERIALS TO TITANIUM THAT YOU
WILL USE IN TEMPERATURES MORE THAN 600°F. IF YOU DO NOT
OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS, DAMAGE TO THE TITANIUM PARTS CAN
OCCUR.
(a) Clean the titanium to remove the oil and other foreign material with solvent, B00094.
1) Do this task: Cleaners and Polishes, TASK 20-30-31-910-801.
(b) Remove the soft hydraulic fluid and the remaining hard hydraulic fluid contamination
(shows as a light glossy, brown film) with cleaner, B00402.
NOTE: The following cleaners are optional to cleaner, B00402: Cee Bee 280 cleaner,
B00005, Oakite 204 cleaner, B00008, and Calla 301A cleaner, B00015.
1) Do this task: Cleaners and Polishes, TASK 20-30-31-910-801.
2) To remove the thick layers of the remaining hard hydraulic fluid contamination, let
the cleaner set for approximately 20 to 40 minutes.
3) After the contamination is soft, remove it with a hard resin phenolic scraper,
STD-1064.
NOTE: Do not use a power brush or abrasive blast to remove the contamination.
a) You can use a light abrasive to remove the remaining dried fluid, do this task:
Miscellaneous Materials, TASK 20-30-51-910-801.
(c) Replace all parts that show paint deterioration and/or metal that is etched.
(d) For gold-plated titanium ducts, also do the following:
1) Clean the gold coated titanium ducts with a lint-free cotton wiper, G00034, and
isopropyl alcohol, B00130.
2) When the duct is clean, you can apply BMS 10-82 low emissivity gold coating,
C00314, to provide a protective coating for the duct.
F. Put the Airplane Back to It's Initial Condition
SUBTASK 05-51-22-400-001
(1) Install the components you removed if they are serviceable.
(a) If the components are not serviceable, install replacement parts.

ATA 05-51-24

05-51-24-200-801Cabin Overpressurization Conditional InspectionPDF p. 989
2. Cabin Overpressurization Conditional Inspection
A. General
(1) Equipment connected to pitot static systems will not be damaged by internal cabin pressure.
(2) Equipment temporarily disconnected from pitot static systems, or carried as spares, may be
damaged by cabin pressure greater than 16 psia (110 kPa).
B. Precautions
(1) If personnel are in the airplane during a test, they must be in good physical condition. If any
person experiences pain during pressure change, you must lower the rate of change of
pressure or make the absolute pressure stable immediately until the person can either make
the pressure equal in their ears, or be removed from the airplane.
NOTE: The ability to adjust to increasing or decreasing pressure is an individual characteristic,
and one which varies from day to day depending upon a person's health. People with
sinus or ear problems should not be exposed to pressure changes. Similarly a person
experiencing headache, toothache, head cold, hay fever, etc., should be excluded
from airplane during test. Individuals subjected to pressure changes should be trained
in techniques for venting the ears.
C. References
Reference Title
35-12-00-800-801 Bleed the Crew Oxygen System Prior to System Maintenance or
Repair (P/B 201)
D. Procedure
SUBTASK 05-51-24-720-001
(1) If a cabin overpressurization occurs that is more than 16 psia (110 kPa), but less than 21 psia
(145 kPa), do the step that follow:
(a) Do a check of all components with pitot static connections that were disconnected, or
carried as spares when the overpressurization occurred.
SUBTASK 05-51-24-720-002
(2) If a cabin overpressurization occurs that is more than 21 psia 145 kPa), do the steps that
follow:
(a) Do the above step for pressurization between 16 and 21 psia (110 and 145 kPa).
(b) Do a check of the oxygen mask regulators from the oxygen system in the crew cabin, do
this task: Bleed the Crew Oxygen System Prior to System Maintenance or Repair,
TASK 35-12-00-800-801.
E. Put the Airplane Back to It's Usual Condition
SUBTASK 05-51-24-410-001
(1) Install the components you removed if they are serviceable, or install replacement parts.

C. Extreme Dust or Sand Conditional Inspection
SUBTASK 05-51-27-200-011
(1) Examine the windshield.
CAUTION
DO NOT OPERATE THE WINDSHIELD WIPERS ON DRY GLASS.
ALWAYS SUPPLY WATER TO THE WINDSHIELDS BEFORE YOU
OPERATE THE WIPER. THE WIPER WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO A DRY
WINDSHIELD.
(a) Make sure that the windshield is free from dust or sand.
SUBTASK 05-51-27-200-007
(2) Examine the surfaces that follow to make sure that they are free from dust or sand.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Fuselage.
(b) Upper surfaces of the wings and other control surfaces.
SUBTASK 05-51-27-200-005
(3) Examine the areas that follow to make sure that they are free from dust or sand.
(a) Probes.
(b) Sensors.
(c) Ports.
1) Including static ports and pitot tubes.
(d) Vents.
(e) Drains.
(f) Left and right ram air inlets.
(g) Cabin pressure outflow valve.
(h) Positive pressure relief valves.
SUBTASK 05-51-27-200-008
(4) Examine the leading edge flaps.
(a) Make sure that they are not damaged.
SUBTASK 05-51-27-200-003
(5) Examine the power plant areas that follow to make sure that they are free from dust or sand.
(a) Engine inlet and cowling.
(b) Indicator probes.
(c) Fan and blades.
1) Make sure that the fan blades are free to turn and are not damaged.
(d) Do the inspection before the next flight if there is dust or sand in the power plant areas
(TASK 71-00-00-200-802-F00).
SUBTASK 05-51-27-200-012
(6) Examine the fuel tank vents.
(a) Make sure that they are free from dust or sand.
SUBTASK 05-51-27-200-002
(7) Examine the landing gear areas that follow to make sure that they are free from dust or sand.
(a) Landing gear shock struts.
(b) Landing gear actuator pushrods.
(c) Landing gear uplock actuator pushrods.
(d) Landing gear doors.
SUBTASK 05-51-27-200-001
(8) Examine the control surfaces that follow to make sure that they are free from dust or sand.
(a) Vertical stabilizer.
(b) Horizontal stabilizer.
(c) Stabilizer trim mechanisms.
(d) Flap screw mechanisms.
(e) Leading edges.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Make sure that all leading edges are not damaged.
SUBTASK 05-51-27-211-001
(9) Visually examine all the exposed portions of the flight control cable.
(a) Make sure that they are free from sand and dust.
SUBTASK 05-51-27-200-010
(10) Examine the Auxiliary Power Unit (APU) areas that follow to make sure that they are free from
dust or sand.
(a) Do the next check to be sure that there is no damage to the APU:
1) Operate the APU on the ground and monitor the pneumatic performance in the
modes that follow:
a) The Main Engine Start (MES) operating mode.
b) The Environmental Control System (ECS) operating mode.
NOTE: Use the applicable APU manufacturer recommendations for engine
inspection for flights through areas of low level dust or sand
concentrations.
(b) Examine the inlet and exhaust ducts for dust or sand contamination.
NOTE: Do not do a borescope inspection on the APU.
1) lf there is dust or sand in the APU inlet or exhaust ducts, look for dust or sand in the
components that follow:
a) Do this task: Oil Cooler Inspection, TASK 49-91-41-200-801.
b) Do this task: Oil Filter Elements Removal, TASK 49-91-12-000-801.
c) Do this task: Inlet Fuel Filter Element Removal, TASK 49-31-21-000-801.
d) Do this task: Exhaust Duct Muffler Inspection, TASK 49-81-11-200-801.
e) Do this task: Bleed Air Duct Removal, TASK 49-52-13-000-801.
SUBTASK 05-51-27-200-004
(11) Examine the air conditioning systems to make sure that they are free from dust or sand.
(a) Do the steps that follow to examine the air conditioning system:
1) Examine the aft outflow valve, do this task: Aft Outflow Valve Assembly Removal,
TASK 21-31-03-000-801.
a) If you find dust or sand in the valve, clean or replace the valve.
2) Remove and examine the negative pressure relief doors, do this task: Negative
Pressure Relief Valve Removal, TASK 21-32-03-000-801.
a) If you find dust or sand in the door area, clean or replace the door and linkage.
3) Remove and examine the positive pressure relief valves, do this task: Positive
Pressure Relief Valve Removal, TASK 21-32-01-000-801.
a) If you find dust or sand in the valves, clean or replace the valves.
4) Remove and examine the positive pressure relief valve filters, do this task: Positive
Pressure Relief Valve Filter Removal, TASK 21-32-02-000-801.
a) If you find dust or sand in the filters, clean or replace the filters.
5) Examine the ram air inlet deflector door, do this task: Ram Air Inlet Deflector Door -
Removal, TASK 21-51-22-000-801.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
a) If you find dust or sand in the deflectors, clean the deflectors and movable
joints.
6) Examine the ram air inlet deflector door shaft assemblies, do this task: Ram Air Inlet
Deflector Door Shaft Assembly - Removal, TASK 21-51-22-000-802.
a) If you find dust or sand in the shaft assemblies, clean the shaft assemblies.
7) Examine the ram air inlet modulation panels, do this task: Ram Air Inlet Modulation
Panels - Removal, TASK 21-51-23-000-801.
a) If you find dust or sand in the modulation panels, clean the panels and
movable joints.
8) Examine the ram air inlet modulation panel shaft assemblies.
a) If you find dust or sand in the shaft assemblies, clean the shaft assemblies.
9) Examine the ram air exhaust modulation louver assemblies.
a) If you find dust or sand in the louver assemblies, clean the louvers, bearings
and movable joints.
10) Examine the ram air inlet actuators, do this task: Ram Air Inlet Actuator Removal,
TASK 21-51-21-000-801.
a) If you find dust or sand in the actuators, clean or replace the actuators.
11) Remove and examine the Air Cycle Machine (ACM), do this task: Air Cycle Machine
Removal, TASK 21-51-04-000-802-002.
a) Check for dust or sand in the ACM valves.
<1> If you find dust or sand in the ACM valves, clean or replace the ACM.
b) If the aircraft has an ACM that was only on a -800 or -900 aircraft, do the steps
that follow:
<1> Remove the high pressure water separator, do this task: High Pressure
Water Separator Removal, TASK 21-51-08-000-802.
<2> Examine the water for contamination.
<3> If there is contamination in the water of the high pressure water
separator, do the steps that follow.
<a> Remove the ACM, do this task: Air Cycle Machine Removal,
TASK 21-51-04-000-802-002.
<b> Inspect the ACM for torus erosion.
NOTE: Torus erosion occurs when atmospheric contamination in
the bleed air is trapped in the ACM torus. This moves
about in the torus and erodes the inner surface of the
torus.
c) If the aircraft has an ACM that was on a -600 or -700 aircraft, do the steps that
follow.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
<1> Inspect the ACM for torus erosion.
NOTE: The high pressure water separator used on the -800 and -900
model airplanes removes contamination with the water prior to
the air entering the ACM turbine. However, if the ACM was
installed on a -600 or -700 model airplane, then used on a -800
or -900 model airplane, the torus wall of the ACM may have
begun to erode prior to being installed on the -800 or -900
airplane.
NOTE: Torus erosion is caused because atmospheric contamination in
the bleed air is trapped in the ACM torus and moves around the
torus, which erodes the inner surface of the torus.
12) Remove and examine the air cycle cooling pack primary and secondary heat
exchangers.
a) If you find dust or sand in the heat exchangers, clean or replace the heat
exchangers.
NOTE: For more information, refer to the applicable manufacturer component
maintenance manual.
13) Examine the water extract nozzles and drain lines.
a) Clean the water extract nozzles and drain lines if dust or sand is found.
14) Remove and examine the condensers, do this task: Condenser Removal,
TASK 21-51-12-000-801.
a) If you find dust or sand in the condensers, clean or replace the condensers.
15) Remove and examine the flow control pack valves, do these tasks: Right Flow
Control and Shutoff Valve - Removal, TASK 21-51-01-000-805-002 or Right Flow
Control and Shutoff Valve Removal, TASK 21-51-01-000-807-003. Left Flow Control
and Shutoff Valve - Removal, TASK 21-51-01-000-802-002 or Left Flow Control and
Shutoff Valve Removal, TASK 21-51-01-000-806-003.
a) If you find dust or sand in the pack valves, clean or replace the pack valves.
16) Remove and examine the recirculating air fans.
a) If you find dust or sand in the fans, clean or replace the fans.
17) Remove and examine one of the trim air nozzles.
a) If you find dust or sand in one of the trim nozzles, remove and clean all of the
trim nozzles.
18) Remove and examine the recirculation air filters.
a) If you find dust or sand in the filters, clean or replace the filters.
19) Remove and examine the recirculation air check valves.
a) If you find dust or sand in the valves, clean or replace the valves.
20) Remove and examine the equipment cooling overboard exhaust valve.
a) If you find dust or sand in the valve, remove or replace the valve.
21) Remove and examine the exhaust fans and check valves.
a) If you find dust or sand in the fans or valves, clean or replace the fans and
valves.
22) Remove and examine the pack temperature control valve.
a) If you find dust or sand in the control valves, clean or replace the valves.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
23) Do a visual examination of the temperature sensors and connectors in both air
conditioning pack bays.
a) Make sure that the temperature sensors and connectors are not damaged and
are installed correctly.
24) Make sure that the flight compartment and cabin temperature sensors are not
clogged.
a) If you find dust or sand in the flight compartment or cabin temperature
sensors, clean or replace the sensors, do this task: Cabin Temperature Sensor
Cleaning, TASK 21-61-10-100-801.
25) Remove and examine the trim air valve.
a) If you find dust or sand in the valves, clean or replace the valves.

(12) Nitrogen Generation System (NGS).

SUBTASK 05-51-27-200-014
(13) Pneumatic System.
(a) Examine the pneumatic system.
1) Do this task: Bleed Air Precooler Removal, TASK 36-12-01-000-801.
2) If you find dust or sand in the bleed air precooler, remove the components that
follow and look for dust or sand.
a) Do this task: High Stage Valve Removal, TASK 36-11-06-000-801.

c) Do this task: Bleed Air Check Valve - Removal, TASK 36-11-02-000-801.
d) Do this task: Start Valve Removal, TASK 80-11-03-000-801-F00.
e) Do this task: Precooler Control Valve Removal, TASK 36-12-02-000-801.

g) Do this task: APU Check Valve Removal, TASK 36-14-02-000-801.
h) Do this task: Ground Pneumatic Connector Check Valve Removal,
TASK 36-13-03-000-801.
i) Do this task: Engine Cowl TAI Valve - Removal, TASK 30-21-11-000-801.
j) Do this task: Duct Pressure Transducer Removal, TASK 36-21-01-000-801.
k) Do this task: High Stage Regulator Removal, TASK 36-11-07-000-801.
l) Do this task: Bleed Air Regulator Removal, TASK 36-11-03-000-801.
m) Do this task: Thermostat Removal, TASK 36-11-05-000-801.
n) Do this task: Precooler Control Valve Sensor Removal,
TASK 36-12-03-000-801.
EFFECTIVITY

SUBTASK 05-51-27-200-015
(14) Fuel System.
(a) Examine the fuel system for dust or sand contamination.
1) Look for dust or sand in a fuel sample from each fuel tank sump, do this task: Fuel
System Sumping, TASK 12-11-00-680-801.
2) Look for dust or sand in a fuel sample from each surge tank sump (if there is fuel in
the surge tanks).
3) Visually inspect for dust or sand in each surge tank, do this task: Surge Tank Access
Door Removal, TASK 28-11-11-000-802.
SUBTASK 05-51-27-200-016
(15) Oxygen System.
(a) If you find dust or sand in the passenger and control cabin, examine the oxygen system.
1) Remove the stowage boxes for the mask and regulator and look for dust or sand,
do this task: Crew Oxygen Stowage Box Test (Mask Stowed in Stowage Box),
TASK 35-12-00-700-801.
2) Examine portable oxygen masks for dust or sand, do this task: Crew Oxygen
Mask-Regulator Test, TASK 35-12-00-700-802.
3) Examine the passenger oxygen masks for dust or sand, do this task: Passenger
Oxygen System - Automatic Actuation Functional Test, TASK 35-22-00-700-801.
SUBTASK 05-51-27-200-017
(16) Potable Water System.
(a) Examine the potable water system for dust or sand contamination.
1) Remove the bleed air filter and look for dust or sand contamination, do this task:
Bleed Air Filter Element Replacement, TASK 38-42-10-960-801.
2) If there is dust or sand in the air filter, do these steps:
a) Visually inspect for dust or sand in a sample from the potable water tanks, do
this task: Potable Water System - Drain, TASK 12-14-01-600-801.
b) Remove the fill/overflow valves and look for dust or sand contamination, do
this task: Fill/Overflow Valve Removal, TASK 38-11-03-000-801.
c) Remove the water quantity transmitters and look for dust or sand
contamination, do this task: Water Quantity Transmitter Removal,
TASK 38-14-01-000-801.
SUBTASK 05-51-27-200-018
(17) Hydraulic System.
(a) Examine the hydraulic system for signs of dust or sand contamination.
1) Visually inspect for dust or sand in a sample of the hydraulic fluid, do this task:
Hydraulic Fluid - Check, TASK 29-11-00-200-801.
D. Clean the Dust or Sand Contamination
SUBTASK 05-51-27-100-001
(1) If you find dust or sand in the areas you examined, remove the dust or sand.
(a) Do this task: Clean (Wet Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane,
TASK 12-40-00-100-801 or Clean (Waterless Wash) the External Surfaces of the
Airplane, TASK 12-40-00-100-803.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
E. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 05-51-27-400-001
(1) Install the components you removed if they are serviceable, or install replacement parts.
(2) Operate the air conditioning packs and check for the conditions that follow:
(a) Unusual noise or vibration.
(b) Leaking on all ducting in the two air conditioning pack bays.

05-51-28-210-801Ice or Snow Condition Maintenance PracticesPDF p. 1001
2. Ice or Snow Condition Maintenance Practices
A. References
Reference Title
12-33-01-600-802 Cold Weather Maintenance Procedure (P/B 301)
B. Location Zones
Zone Area
100 Lower Half of Fuselage
200 Upper Half of Fuselage
300 Empennage
500 Left Wing
600 Right Wing
C. Procedure
SUBTASK 05-51-28-210-001
(1) When there are ice or snow conditions, examine the airplane.
(a) Look at the areas that follow for ice or snow:
1) the fuselage.
2) the wings.
3) the TE flaps.
4) the LE flaps.
5) the LE slats.
6) the ailerons.
7) the stabilizers.
8) the elevators.
9) the rudder.
10) the accessible areas of the balance panels.
11) the accessible areas of control surface hinge points and hinges.
12) the gaps between wing structure and aileron nose.
13) the gaps between fin and rudder nose.
14) the gaps between horizontal stabilizer and elevator nose.
15) the engine fan blades.
(b) The areas that follow must not have any snow or ice on them before takeoff:
1) the total area of wing upper surface.
2) the wing leading edge.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
3) all control surfaces.
4) all tab surfaces.
5) balance panel cavities.
6) the engine fan blades.
(c) Look in the engine inlet cowl for ice and snow.
1) Make sure the fan turns freely.
2) If there is ice on the engine fan blades, do this task: Cold Weather Maintenance
Procedure, TASK 12-33-01-600-802
SUBTASK 05-51-28-610-001
(2) If there is ice, snow, slush, and/or frost, do the step that follows:
(a) Do this task: Cold Weather Maintenance Procedure, TASK 12-33-01-600-802.

B. Location Zones
Zone Area
700 Landing Gear and Landing Gear Doors
C. Nose Landing Gear Area, Exceeding Maximum Steering Angle, Maximum Towing Load.
Figure 09-11-00-990-803
SUBTASK 05-51-29-200-001
(1) Examine the nose landing gear areas that follow:
(a) The tires, do this task: Tires - Inspection, TASK 32-45-00-700-803.
(b) The wheels, do this task: Wheels Fast Check (Wheel Installed on the Airplane),
TASK 32-45-00-700-801.
1) If the examination finds any wheels damaged, do this task: (Wheels Inspection
(Wheel Removed from the Airplane), TASK 32-45-00-700-802).
(c) If damage occurred during towing with or without a towbar, do these steps:
1) Verify the axle is not bent or deformed.
2) Examine the axle threads for excessive damage.
3) Examine the following pins for signs of crank shafting, cracks or other gross defects:
a) Torsion Link Pin, upper
b) Torsion Link Pin, lower
c) Torsion Link Pin, apex
d) Steering Collar Pins
(d) Make sure all of the fasteners are installed in the correct positions.
(e) Make sure there are no loose fasteners in the web of the nose wheel well near the
trunnion support.
(f) Examine the steering cable control system for signs of cable overload, do this task:
Inspect Nose Gear Steering Cables, TASK 32-51-31-220-801.
1) Verify the pulley brackets are not deformed.
2) Verify the proper cable rigging.
(g) Examine the nose gear steering actuator rods for signs of necking or contact with the
steering collar .
1) Verify the actuator rods are not bent.
(h) Examine the actuator rod end attachments to the steering collar for signs of deformation
and excessive freeplay.
(i) Examine the actuator trunnion attachments to the steering plates for signs of deformation
and excessive freeplay.
(j) Examine the nose gear torque links for signs of deformation and excessive freeplay.
(k) Operationally check the steering system by commanding slow tiller inputs in both
directions.
1) Verify no system binding occurs and there is no leakage from steering actuator
trunnions and rod seals and steering metering valve.
(l) Examine the upper and lower ends of the shock strut of the nose gear for fluid leakage.
(m) Examine the outer cylinder of the nose landing gear.
(n) Examine the nose landing gear inner cylinder at tow fittings.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(o) Examine the nose landing gear inner cylinder torsion links attach lugs.
(p) Examine the nose landing gear trunnions for signs of damage.
(q) Examine the nose landing gear trunnion attachment areas.
1) Examine bolted connections (attaching upper end of outer cylinder and upper end of
upper drag brace).
(r) Examine both upper and lower drag brace segments, attach lugs, and pins.
(s) Examine the doors, hinges and retraction mechanism of the nose landing gear and the
nose landing gear taxi light bracket for signs of damage.
05-51-29-200-802Phase II InspectionPDF p. 1005
3. Phase II Inspection
A. References
Reference Title
12-15-41-610-802 Nose Landing Gear Shock Strut Servicing, Airplane on the
Ground (P/B 301)

(P/B 501)
32-51-00-700-801 Nose Wheel Steering System Test (P/B 501)
B. Location Zones
Zone Area
700 Landing Gear and Landing Gear Doors
C. Nose Landing Gear Operational Check
SUBTASK 05-51-29-200-002
(1) Retract and then extend the nose landing gear with the normal system to make sure it
operates correctly.
(a) Do this task: Operational Test for the Nose Landing Gear, TASK 32-33-00-710-801.
(b) Retract and then extend the nose landing gear with the manual system to make sure it
operate correctly.
1) Do this task: Nose Gear Manual Extension System Test - Airplane on Jacks,
TASK 32-35-00-730-801.
D. Nose Landing Gear Inspections
SUBTASK 05-51-29-200-003
(1) Examine the nose landing gear areas that follow:
(a) Do this task: Nose Landing Gear Inspection, TASK 32-21-00-200-801.
(b) Do this task: Nose Landing Gear Torsional Freeplay Inspection, TASK 32-21-00-700-801.
(c) Examine the shock strut of the nose landing gear for fluid leakage.
(d) Examine the shock strut of the nose landing gear to make sure the pressure is
satisfactory.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Do this task: Nose Landing Gear Shock Strut Servicing, Airplane on the Ground,
TASK 12-15-41-610-802.
(e) Remove the inner cylinder if:
1) There is visible damage to any of the following structural components:
a) Nose landing gear inner cylinder.
b) Nose landing gear outer cylinder
c) Drag strut
2) There are signs of a shock strut fluid leak.
3) It is known the maximum towing load has been exceeded.
(f) If you remove the inner cylinder, examine the inner cylinder as follows:
1) Perform a visual examination looking for distortion and cracks.
2) Do a dimensional inspection.
3) Do an NDT inspection, if appropriate.
(g) Do a check of the rigging of the steering mechanism.
1) Do this task: Nose Wheel Steering System Test, TASK 32-51-00-700-801.

05-51-31-210-801Volcanic Ash Operational Encounter Conditional InspectionPDF p. 1007
2. Volcanic Ash Operational Encounter Conditional Inspection
A. General
(1) This inspection is divided into three phases (Phase I, Phase II and Phase III).
(a) Phase I (IA and IB) is a general visual inspection for one or more of the following:
1) The flight crew reported the airplane flight path was through a cloud of visual
volcanic ash.
2) The airplane lands or takes off in volcanic ash fallout conditions.
NOTE: Fallout is identified as ash drifting down from the air, or is blown about by
the wind. Fallout is also caused by the ash being blown or moved about
because of the movement of airplanes and ramp vehicles.
3) An airplane encounters volcanic ash while operating on the ground during volcanic
ash fallout conditions.
(b) Phase II is applicable when any of the Phase IB inspections show positive results.
(c) Phase III is applicable when any of the Phase II inspections show positive results.
(2) Volcanic ash has the qualities that follow:
(a) It is hard and highly abrasive.
(b) It usually contains trace chemicals which can be acidic (pH between 2 and neutral).
(c) It can cause erosion/abrasion, etching or shot peening on exposed surfaces and remove
protective finishes.
(d) The dimensions of most ash particles are less than 5 microns with trace amounts that are
more than 50 microns.
(e) It resembles talcum powder.
(f) It stays on exposed lubricated surfaces.
(g) Able to enter small orifices and pass by seals.
(h) Can cause unusual wear and contamination of many airplane systems and filter
elements.
WARNING
DO NOT GET VOLCANIC ASH IN YOUR MOUTH, EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN.
PUT ON A RESPIRATOR MASK THAT REMOVES VOLCANIC ASH PARTICLES
SUFFICIENTLY. PUT ON CLOTHES AND GOGGLES (OR OTHER APPROVED
EYE PROTECTION) THAT KEEP VOLCANIC ASH OFF YOU. VOLCANIC ASH
CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(3) Volcanic ash can cause discomfort and injury to persons during fallout conditions, and during
inspection and cleaning.
(a) Precautions must be followed when you work in a volcanic ash environment. This will
prevent the entry of volcanic ash into your eyes and your respiratory (breathing) system.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(4) Guidance for flight through areas of low level volcanic ash concentrations.
(a)  guidance is to always avoid operation in visible ash.
(b) For operations in low volcanic ash concentrations (not visible), the Airframe and Systems
can handle these operations without requiring unique or special inspections outside the
normal operating and maintenance experience of individual airlines.
(c) Airframe and systems degradation can occur at different rates within many operating
environments. As this normal degradation occurs and varies between operating
environments, airlines typically adjust their maintenance practices to ensure airplane
degradation (e.g. plugged heat exchangers, filters, abrasions, etc.) doesn’t cause
unscheduled airplane downtime. This same maintenance philosophy applies to
operations in low levels of ash concentrations. A continuous operation in areas of low
level volcanic ash concentrations is of interest to  in collecting operator
observations and experiences. If significant observations are discovered beyond normal
variations currently known,  will share these observations and any improved
recommendations for maintenance practices. The diagram in Fig. 201 illustrates general
areas where  recommends increased observation during normal hanger visits, and
potential temporary adjustments for maintenance programs based on the observations, to
prevent unscheduled maintenance. Observations should include signs of unusual or
accelerated abrasions and / or ash accumulation.
(5) Volcanic ash encounters can show these properties inside the engine:
(a) As the ash goes through the combustor, it can change from ash to a glass material in a
plastic flow or a molten condition.
(b) In the molten condition, the ash will have very high adhesive qualities.
1) The ash will bond to the nozzle guide vanes of the high pressure turbine.
2) The ash will also bond to the rotor blades of the high pressure turbine.
a) When the ash bonds to these components, it causes a decrease in the turbine
flow area.
b) The ash also causes a decrease of nozzle guide vane and turbine blade
cooling air.
(c) It may obstruct fuel injectors and cause engine shutdown.
(d) Ash usually accumulates in the turbine section and can continue to cause damage unless
fully cleaned.
(e) Ash can cause erosion of the High Pressure Compressor (HPC) airfoils.
(6) Indicators for the flight crew that an airplane has encountered volcanic ash in flight are related
to odor, visibility, haze, changing engine conditions, airspeed, pressurization, and static
discharges.
(a) Odor - When encountering a volcanic ash cloud, flight crews usually notice a smoky or
acrid odor that can smell like electrical smoke, burned dust, or sulfur.
1) Smoke or dust appearing in the flight deck which may cause the flight crew to don
oxygen masks.
(b) Visibility - Flight deck windshields become opaque with limited or no view.
(c) Haze - Flight crews, as well as cabin crews and passengers, can see a haze develop
within the airplane. Dust can settle on surfaces.
1) Sharp distinct shadows cast by landing lights as compared to the diffused shadows
observed in clouds.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(d) Changing engine conditions - Surging, torching from the tailpipe, and flameouts can
occur. Engine temperatures can change unexpectedly and a white or orange glow can
appear at the engine inlets.
1) Multiple engine malfunctions, such as stalls, increasing Exhaust Gas Temperature
(EGT), torching, flameout, and loss of thrust causing immediate departure from
assigned altitude.
2) On engine restart attempts, engines may accelerate to idle very slowly, especially at
high altitudes.
(e) Airspeed - If volcanic ash fouls the pitot tube, the indicated airspeed can decrease or
fluctuate erratically.
(f) Pressurization - Cabin pressure can change, including possible loss of cabin
pressurization.
(g) Static discharges – An electrostatic discharge/St. Elmo’s Fire or glow can occur. In these
instances, blue-colored sparks can appear to flow up the outside of the windshield or a
white glow can appear at the leading edges of the wings or at the front of the engine
inlets.
1) An electrostatic discharge/St. Elmo’s Fire around the windshields.
NOTE: This electrical discharge is often referred as St. Elmo's Fire, which is an
electrical weather phenomenon where luminous plasma is created by a
coronal discharge originating from a grounded object in an atmospheric
electric field (such as those generated by thunderstorms or thunderstorms
created by a volcanic explosion).
2) A bright glow in the engine inlets along with subsequent engine shutdown.
(7) The following is a guide to help identify positive volcanic ash results versus false positive
results. Minimum experience inspecting for volcanic ash may induce a number of probable
results which have not been recognized previously, but are well known results caused by
normal operation.
(a) results caused by in-flight volcanic ash encounters are usually symmetrically on both
sides of the airplane.
NOTE: Positive results on one side of the airplane can be from single engine taxi ground
operations or operation through ash that is not uniform thickness.
(b) If there are signs of volcanic ash on one engine, the other engine(s) should show the
same signs.
1) For example, results in one pack system should be similar on all packs.
2) For example, an engine spinner or inlet lip skin shows abrasion, the other engine(s)
should show similar abrasion.
(c) Volcanic ash typically has a light grey color and looks like talcum powder.
(d) Black or dark debris on the aircraft skin, engine and fan blades are normal debris usually
caused by industrial dust.
(e) Yellow or green debris inside of pitot tubes and/or similar sensors may are typical of plant
pollen.
(f) White debris on acoustic panels of the engine inlet, fan blades, outlet guide vanes etc.
can be residuals of water.
(g) White signs on the fuselage and wings can be caused by aircraft dry cleaning.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(h) A check of the maintenance history in the area of your results may indicate residual
material from recent maintenance.
1) For example, a relubrication of the fan blades may also cause unusual debris on
spinner, blades and engine inlet.

D. Phase IA General Visual Inspection
SUBTASK 05-51-31-210-018
(1) Do a visual inspection of the airframe for abrasion damage:
(a) Radome for unusual abrasion
(b) Wing leading edges, landing lights and navlight glazings for unusual abrasion or crazing.
(c) Cockpit windows for unusual abrasion, cracking, crazing, discoloration or decreased
visibility.
(d) Landing gear painted surfaces for abrasion.
(e) Pack ram air inlets for unusual abrasion.
SUBTASK 05-51-31-210-020
(2) Do a visual inspection of the sensors and probes for abrasion damage:
(a) Angle of Attack (AOA) sensors for unusual abrasion and free movement
(b) TAT probes for unusual abrasion
(c) Pitot tubes for unusual abrasion
(d) Static ports for unusual abrasion.
SUBTASK 05-51-31-210-021
(3) Do a visual inspection of the following areas for ash contamination:
(a) Engine inlet lip skins, fan blades, and spinners
(b) Pitot probes and static ports
(c) Drain holes (bilge drains and engine drains)
(d) Lubricated surfaces (actuator rams, landing gear inner cylinders)
(e) Pack ram air inlets.
SUBTASK 05-51-31-210-022
(4) Do a visual inspection of the Auxiliary Power Unit (APU) for damage:
NOTE: Inspection can be performed from ground level.
NOTE: Use the applicable APU manufacturer recommendations for engine inspection for
flights through areas of low level volcanic ash concentrations.
(a) APU inlet for unusual abrasion
(b) APU exhaust for unusual abrasion
(c) APU drains for abnormal conditions such as excessive or unexpected fuel or oil drainage.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 05-51-31-210-023
(5) Do a visual inspection of each engine for damage:
NOTE: Use the applicable engine manufacturer recommendations for engine inspection and
sampling for flights through areas of low level volcanic ash concentrations.
(a) Engine nose cowl inlet lips for unusual abrasion
(b) Engine spinner for unusual abrasion
(c) Fan Outlet Guide Vane (OGV)s leading edge for unusual abrasion (through fan blades).
SUBTASK 05-51-31-210-024
(6) If any of the Phase IA inspections show positive results, then the Phase IB inspection must be
completed before the next flight.
NOTE: Typically, damage from volcanic ash encounters occur symmetrically on both sides of
the aircraft. You may also extend the visual inspections to leading edges of stabilizers,
antennae etc., as far as visible from ground, to confirm the inspection results.
E. Phase IB General Visual Inspection
SUBTASK 05-51-31-200-001
(1) Borescope first stages of HPC and High Pressure Turbine (HPT) blades for unusual abrasion
or ash deposit on one engine.
(a) If the one engine does not show signs of unusual abrasion or grey dust accumulation, the
other engine(s) do not need to be inspected.
SUBTASK 05-51-31-200-004
(2) If any of the Phase IB inspections show positive results, then the Phase II inspection must be
completed before the next flight.
F. Phase II Inspection
SUBTASK 05-51-31-200-002
(1) Engines
(a) Do the steps that follow to examine each engine.
1) Examine each engine for damage, do this task: Inspection of the Engine After
Volcanic Ash, Dust or Sand Ingestion, TASK 71-00-00-200-802-F00.
2) Examine the engine control mechanisms and linkages for volcanic ash.
a) Examine the Variable Stator Vane (VSV) and Variable Bleed Valve (VBV)
systems for volcanic ash.
NOTE: These are mechanically controlled by a series of linkages to adjust the
airflow through the engine.
b) Examine the High Pressure Turbine Active Clearance Control (HPTACC) and
Low Pressure Turbine Active Clearance Control (LPTACC) valves and tubing
for volcanic ash.
(b) If any of the Phase II inspections show positive results, then the Phase III inspection must
be completed before the next flight.
G. Phase III
SUBTASK 05-51-31-200-003
(1) Examine the Air Condition Systems
(a) Do the steps that follow to examine the air conditioning system:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Examine the aft outflow valve, do this task: Aft Outflow Valve Assembly Removal,
TASK 21-31-03-000-801.
a) If you find volcanic ash in the valve, clean or replace the valve.
2) Remove and examine the negative pressure relief doors, do this task: Negative
Pressure Relief Valve Removal, TASK 21-32-03-000-801.
a) If you find volcanic ash in the door area, clean or replace the door and linkage.
3) Remove and examine the positive pressure relief valves, do this task: Positive
Pressure Relief Valve Removal, TASK 21-32-01-000-801.
a) If you find volcanic ash in the valves, clean or replace the valves.
4) Remove and examine the positive pressure relief valve filters, do this task: Positive
Pressure Relief Valve Filter Removal, TASK 21-32-02-000-801.
a) If you find volcanic ash in the filters, clean or replace the filters.
5) Examine the ram air inlet deflector door, do this task: Ram Air Inlet Deflector Door -
Removal, TASK 21-51-22-000-801.
a) If you find volcanic ash in the deflectors, clean the deflectors and movable
joints.
6) Examine the ram air inlet deflector door shaft assemblies, do this task: Ram Air Inlet
Deflector Door Shaft Assembly - Removal, TASK 21-51-22-000-802.
a) If you find volcanic ash in the shaft assemblies, clean the shaft assemblies.
7) Examine the ram air inlet modulation panels, do this task: Ram Air Inlet Modulation
Panels - Removal, TASK 21-51-23-000-801.
a) If you find volcanic ash in the modulation panels, clean the panels and
movable joints.
8) Examine the ram air inlet modulation panel shaft assemblies.
a) If you find volcanic ash in the shaft assemblies, clean the shaft assemblies.
9) Examine the ram air exhaust modulation louver assemblies.
a) If you find volcanic ash in the louver assemblies, clean the louvers, bearings
and movable joints.
10) Examine the ram air inlet actuators, do this task: Ram Air Inlet Actuator Removal,
TASK 21-51-21-000-801.
a) If you find volcanic ash in the actuators, clean or replace the actuators.
11) Remove and examine the Air Cycle Machine (ACM)s, do this task: Air Cycle
Machine Removal, TASK 21-51-04-000-802-002.
a) Check for volcanic ash in the ACM valves.
<1> If you find volcanic ash in the ACM valves, clean or replace the ACM.
b) If the aircraft has an ACM that was only on a -800 or -900 aircraft, do the steps
that follow.
<1> Remove the high pressure water separator, do this task: High Pressure
Water Separator Removal, TASK 21-51-08-000-802.
<2> Examine the water for contamination.
<3> If there is contamination in the water of the high pressure water
separator, do the steps that follow.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
<a> Remove the ACM, do this task: Air Cycle Machine Removal,
TASK 21-51-04-000-802-002.
<b> Inspect the ACM for torus erosion.
NOTE: Torus erosion is caused because atmospheric
contamination in the bleed air is trapped in the ACM
torus and moves around the torus, which erodes the
inner surface of the torus.
c) If the aircraft has an ACM that was on a -600 or -700 aircraft, do the steps that
follow.
<1> Inspect the ACM for torus erosion.
NOTE: The high pressure water separator used on the -800 and -900
model airplanes removes contamination with the water prior to
the air entering the ACM turbine. However, if the ACM was
installed on a -600 or -700 model airplane, then used on a -800
or -900 model airplane, the torus wall of the ACM may have
begun to erode prior to being installed on the -800 or -900
airplane.
NOTE: Torus erosion is caused because atmospheric contamination in
the bleed air is trapped in the ACM torus and moves around the
torus, which erodes the inner surface of the torus.
12) Remove and examine the air cycle cooling pack primary and secondary heat
exchangers.
a) If you find volcanic ash in the heat exchangers, clean or replace the heat
exchangers.
NOTE: For more information, refer to the Honeywell CMM 21-50-14.
13) Make sure that the heat exchanger passes the Pressure Flow Tests to verify that
the unit is fully cleaned and not clogged.
a) Do this every 2000-3000 hours.
14) Examine the water extract nozzles and drain lines.
a) Clean the water extract nozzles and drain lines if volcanic ash is found.
15) Remove and examine the condensers, do this task: Condenser Removal,
TASK 21-51-12-000-801.
a) If you find volcanic ash in the condensers, clean or replace the condensers.
16) Remove and examine the flow control pack valves, do this task: Left Flow Control
and Shutoff Valve Removal, TASK 21-51-01-000-806-003 or Right Flow Control and
Shutoff Valve - Removal, TASK 21-51-01-000-805-002 or Right Flow Control and
Shutoff Valve Removal, TASK 21-51-01-000-807-003 or Left Flow Control and
Shutoff Valve - Removal, TASK 21-51-01-000-802-002.
a) If you find volcanic ash in the pack valves, clean or replace the pack valves.
17) Remove and examine the recirculating air fans.
a) If you find volcanic ash in the fans, clean or replace the fans.
18) Remove and examine one of the trim air nozzles.
a) If you find volcanic ash in one of the trim nozzles, remove and clean all of the
trim nozzles.
19) Remove and examine the recirculation air filters.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
a) If you find volcanic ash in the filters, clean or replace the filters.
20) Remove and examine the recirculation air check valves.
a) If you find volcanic ash in the valves, clean or replace the valves.
21) Remove and examine the equipment cooling automatic flow control valve.
a) If you find volcanic ash in the valve, remove or replace the valve.
22) Remove and examine the exhaust fans and check valves.
a) If you find volcanic ash in the fans or valves, clean or replace the fans and
valves.
23) Remove and examine the pack temperature control valve.
a) If you find volcanic ash in the control valves, clean or replace the valves.
24) Do a visual examination of the temperature sensors and connectors in both air
conditioning pack bays.
a) Make sure that the temperature sensors and connectors are not damaged and
are installed correctly.
25) Make sure that the flight compartment and cabin temperature sensors are not
clogged.
a) If you find volcanic ash in the flight compartment or cabin temperature
sensors, clean or replace the sensors, do this task: Cabin Temperature Sensor
Cleaning, TASK 21-61-10-100-801.
26) Remove and examine the trim air valve.
a) If you find volcanic ash in the valves, clean or replace the valves.

05-51-31-200-801Volcanic Ash Ground Fallout Conditional InspectionPDF p. 1024
3. Volcanic Ash Ground Fallout Conditional Inspection
A. General
(1) This task has information to examine a parked airplane for contamination in volcanic ash fallout
conditions.
(2) Fallout is identified as ash drifting down from the air, or is blown about by the wind. Fallout is
also caused by the ash being blown or moved about because of the movement of airplanes
and ramp vehicles.
(3) For airplanes parked in fallout conditions, protect all inlets of systems, probes, static ports,
engines, gaps, etc. with suitable covers.
(a) Any covered areas should have appropriate streamers or markings, to be removed
before operation.
(4) Volcanic ash has the qualities that follow:
(a) It is hard and highly abrasive.
(b) It usually contains trace chemicals which can be acidic (pH between 2 and neutral).
(c) It can cause erosion/abrasion, etching or shot peening on exposed surfaces and remove
protective finishes.
(d) The dimensions of most ash particles are less than 5 microns with trace amounts that are
more than 50 microns.
(e) It resembles talcum powder.
(f) It stays on exposed lubricated surfaces.
(g) Able to enter small orifices and pass by seals.
(h) Can cause unusual wear and contamination of many airplane systems and filter
elements.
WARNING
DO NOT GET VOLCANIC ASH IN YOUR MOUTH, EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN.
PUT ON A RESPIRATOR MASK THAT REMOVES VOLCANIC ASH PARTICLES
SUFFICIENTLY. PUT ON CLOTHES AND GOGGLES (OR OTHER APPROVED
EYE PROTECTION) THAT KEEP VOLCANIC ASH OFF YOU. VOLCANIC ASH
CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(5) Volcanic ash can cause discomfort and injury to persons during fallout conditions, and during
inspection and cleaning.
(a) Precautions must be followed when you work in a volcanic ash environment. This will
prevent the entry of volcanic ash into your eyes and your respiratory (breathing) system.
(6) The following is a guide to help identify positive volcanic ash findings versus false positive
findings. Minimum experience inspecting for volcanic ash may induce a number of probable
findings which have not been recognized previously, but are well known findings caused by
normal operation.
(a) Black or dark debris on the aircraft skin, engine and fan blades are normal debris usually
caused by industrial dust.
(b) Yellow or green debris inside of pitot tubes and/or similar sensors may are typical of plant
pollen.
(c) White debris on acoustic panels of the engine inlet, fan blades, outlet guide vanes etc.
can be residuals of water.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(d) White signs on the fuselage and wings can be caused by aircraft dry cleaning.
(e) A check of the maintenance history in the area of your findings may indicate residual
material from recent maintenance.
1) For example, a relubrication of the fan blades may also cause unusual debris on
spinner, blades and engine inlet.
B. References
Reference Title
12-40-00-100-805 Clean the Exterior Surface of Volcanic and Fire Ash (P/B 201)
C. Procedure
SUBTASK 05-51-31-211-001
(1) Examine the airplane exterior surfaces and the area (ground, service equipment, buildings)
around the airplane for any indication of ash.
(a) If no ash is found, no more inspection or cleaning is necessary.
(2) If any ash is found, remove all traces of the ash, including areas such as the fuselage crown,
horizontal surfaces, inlets, wheel wells, and exposed chrome common to landing gear.
(a) Do this task: Clean the Exterior Surface of Volcanic and Fire Ash,
TASK 12-40-00-100-805.
SUBTASK 05-51-31-210-019
(3) Make sure the area around the airplane is free from ash.
NOTE: Coordinate with the local airport authority to make sure the ramps, taxiways, and
runways are clear from ash contamination.

2. Tail Strike Inspection
A. References
Reference Title

51-21-99 P/B 701 DECORATIVE EXTERIOR PAINT SYSTEM -
CLEANING/PAINTING
B. Location Zones
Zone Area
100 Lower Half of Fuselage
144 Area Below Aft Cargo Compartment - Right
145 Aft Cargo Compartment Equipment Bay - Left
310 Fuselage - Body Station 1016.00 to Body Station 1217.00
C. Tail Strike Inspection Procedure
SUBTASK 05-51-32-210-003
(1) Examine the tail skid assembly drag shoe for tail strike damage as follows:
(a) Do this task: Tail Skid Inspection, TASK 05-51-32-210-802.
(b) If there is no damage to the bottom of the fuselage and you do not have to replace the
crushable cartridge, it is not necessary to continue with the Tail Strike Inspection.
Continue to Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition.
SUBTASK 05-51-32-210-005
(2) Inspect the external skin surfaces of the lower aft fuselage.
(a) Look from station 947 (approximate aft of the cargo bay aft bulkhead) to the APU
compartment.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Look at the following areas for broken, bent, (distorted), missing parts or other
damage:
a) The APU firewall
b) The APU drain
c) The doors of the APU compartment
d) The drain mast.
2) Inspect the upper fuselage structure aft of the wing rear spar for buckled structure,
cracks and paint that has flaked.
(b) Inspect for fasteners that are loose or missing.
SUBTASK 05-51-32-200-001
(3) Examine all of the external and internal structure of the fuselage, section 48, Body Station
(BSTA) 1016, that you can get access to and/or is called out in this procedure for signs of
buckling, deformation or damage.
NOTE: Look at the structure from the rear pressure bulkhead to the aft end of the airplane.
(a) Do a detailed visual inspection of the exterior fuselage skin 10 in. (25.4 cm) forward and
aft of the BSTA 1016 skin butt joint between stringers S-10L and S-10R.
NOTE: Gain access to the exterior of the fuselage skin at BS 1016 under the vertical
stabilizer fairing, 323AL and 323AR.
(b) Do a detailed visual inspection of the entire aft side of the BSTA 1016 aft pressure
bulkhead.
1) Give particular attention to the upper bulkhead structure between skin stringers
S-10L and S-10R.
NOTE: Access to the interior unpressurized aft pressure bulkhead area is through
the aft access hatch, 311BL.
SUBTASK 05-51-32-210-007
(4) When you find external damage, inspect the fuselage internally as follows:
(a) In the area of the tail strike:
1) Inspect for bent or cracked stringers, frames, or clips.
2) Inspect for buckled or wrinkled webs.
3) Inspect for loose or missing fasteners and paint that has flaked.
4) Inspect the lower area of the aft pressure bulkhead for damage.
(b) Aft pressure bulkhead at BSTA 1016:
1) Examine at BSTA 1016 the upper center web installation on the forward side of the
pressure bulkhead for any damage.
NOTE: Gain access to inspect the upper center web installation by removing the
galley and lavatories as necessary.
SUBTASK 05-51-32-800-001
(5) If damage is found in the above paragraphs, use the applicable Structural Repair Manual
(SRM) and do the repairs.
D. Stabilizer Position Indicator System Procedure
SUBTASK 05-51-32-210-008
(1) Inspect the stabilizer position indication system components, do this task: Stabilizer Manual
Trim and Trim Indicator - Test, TASK 27-41-00-700-801.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Inspect for broken cables.
(b) Inspect for cables that are out of the pulley groove.
(c) When there is no internal damage to the fuselage structure, do the operational test for the
stabilizer position indication system.
1) Do this task: Stabilizer Control Mechanism Detail Visual Inspection,
TASK 27-41-41-210-801.
2) Do this task: Stabilizer Manual Trim and Trim Indicator - Test,
TASK 27-41-00-700-801.
(d) When there is internal damage to the fuselage structure, do the system test for the
stabilizer position indicating system.
SUBTASK 05-51-32-210-009
(2) If the stabilizer position indicating system components are damaged:
(a) Do this task: Horizontal Stabilizer - Removal, TASK 27-41-11-000-801
(b) Do this task: Horizontal Stabilizer Installation, TASK 27-41-11-400-801.
E. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 05-51-32-410-002
(1) Install all of the components you removed if the components are serviceable, or install
replacement parts.
SUBTASK 05-51-32-370-001
(2) If the tail skid drag shoe is within tolerance and the paint finish on the lower surface of the tail
skid drag shoe has been gouged or scratched by contact with the runway, paint the skid drag
shoe in accordance with the Decorative Exterior Finishes procedure (DECORATIVE
EXTERIOR PAINT SYSTEM - CLEANING/PAINTING, PAGEBLOCK 51-21-99/701).
NOTE: If the tail skid drag shoe scratch or gouge damage is not painted over, a person may
interpret the damage as new and request an unnecessary inspection. The addition of
paint can help to determine when new tail strikes have occurred.
SUBTASK 05-51-32-200-005
(3) Make sure that pressurization mode selector is in the AUTO position.

C. Tail Skid Inspection
SUBTASK 05-51-32-210-010
(1) Inspect the external tail drag surfaces.
NOTE: The cartridge assembly warning placard must be examined as soon as possible after
the tail strike. The skirt fairing for the tail skid does not extend again because of gravity
as a result of time.
(a) Visually inspect the tail skid and skin surfaces of the lower aft fuselage, do this task:
Tailskid Shoe Inspection, TASK 32-71-00-900-801.
1) Make sure that the tail drag shoe is serviceable and within tolerance limits.
(b) Make sure that the crushable cartridge is within serviceable limits, do this task: Tailskid
Cartridge Assembly - Inspection/Check, TASK 32-71-00-200-801.
(c) Inspect the tailskid drag assembly for cracks or fractures.
(d) Examine the tail skid fuse pin for signs of shear.
(e) Inspect from zone 140 to the APU compartment for signs of the conditions that follow:
NOTE: This inspection is the lower area of Section 47 and 48.
1) Look for signs of scrapes and cracked or buckled belly skin. Also look for fasteners
that are loose or are not there:
a) scrapes
b) holes
c) cracked skin
d) burns
e) buckled belly skin
f) loose fasteners
g) missing fasteners.
SUBTASK 05-51-32-210-012
(2) Inspect the internal tail drag surfaces.
(a) When you find external damage, examine the fuselage internally in the area of the tail
drag.
(b) Look for bent or cracked:
1) stringers
2) frames
3) clips
4) wrinkled webs
5) look for loose or missing fasteners.
(c) Examine the lower area of the aft pressure bulkhead for damage.
SUBTASK 05-51-32-800-003
(3) If you find internal or external damage, use the applicable Structural Repair Manual (SRM) for
the repairs.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 05-51-32-200-003
(4) If you found damage to the bottom of the fuselage, or you have to replace the crushable
cartridge, do this task: Tail Strike Inspection, TASK 05-51-32-210-801.
NOTE: It is not necessary to repeat inspection steps that have already been performed as part
of the tail skid inspection procedure.
SUBTASK 05-51-32-200-004
(5) Examine the tail skid warning decal.
(a) If missing, do this task: Replacement of the Tail Skid Warning Decal,
TASK 32-71-00-960-803.
D. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 05-51-32-410-003
(1) Install all of the components you removed if they are serviceable, or install replacement parts.
SUBTASK 05-51-32-200-006
(2) Make sure that pressurization mode selector is in the AUTO position.

C. Winglet Strike Inspection Procedure.
SUBTASK 05-51-36-211-001
(1) Remove the damaged winglet (Winglet Removal, TASK 57-21-21-000-801).
(a) Do a detailed visual inspection of the winglet to wing attachments.
SUBTASK 05-51-36-211-002
(2) Do a detailed visual inspection of the closure rib for evidence of cracks, buckling, elongated
holes or other damage.
NOTE: Use 10x magnification around the winglet attach fastener holes.
SUBTASK 05-51-36-211-003
(3) Do a detailed visual inspection to these areas, for evidence of cracking, buckling or other
damage:
(a) Closure rib forward and aft attach fitting.
(b) Adjacent areas of the front and rear spar including chords and web from both the forward
and aft sides.
SUBTASK 05-51-36-211-004
(4) Do a detailed visual inspection of the upper and lower inspar skins adjacent to the closure rib
for evidence of cracking or buckling.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 05-51-36-250-001
(5) Do a high frequency eddy current inspection of each winglet attach bolt hole in the closure rib
and the bolt holes common to the forward and aft rib attach fittings (737 NDT Part 6, 51-00-00,
Procedure 16).
(a) Make sure no cracks exist.

examinations will be performed.

and tires prevents the recovery and/or movement of the airplane to the prepared

05-51-48-211-801Fuel Imbalance Exceedance - Conditional InspectionPDF p. 1053
2. Fuel Imbalance Exceedance - Conditional Inspection
A. General
(1) The Airplane Flight Manual (AFM) for the 737 models identifies that the lateral fuel imbalance
between main wing tanks must be scheduled to be zero. Random fuel imbalance between
main wing tanks for towing, taxi, takeoff, flight, or landing is limited to 1000 lb (454 kg).
Operators experiencing fuel imbalances greater than 1000 lb (454 kg) should review the below
criteria for evaluation of what maintenance actions or structural inspections are required.
B. References
Reference Title
05-51-01 P/B 201 HARD LANDING OR OVERWEIGHT/HARD LANDING OR
HIGH DRAG/SIDE LOAD CONDITION - MAINTENANCE
PRACTICES (CONDITIONAL INSPECTION)
05-51-04-210-801 Severe or Unusual Turbulence, Excessive Maneuver, Buffet, or
Speeds More than the Design Limits Conditional Inspection
(P/B 201)
C. Location Zones
Zone Area
131 Center Section Wing Box, Body Station 540.00 to Body Station 663.75 - Left
132 Center Section Wing Box, Body Station 540.00 to Body Station 663.75 - Right
531 Left Wing - Center Fuel Tank, Rib 1 to Rib 5
532 Left Wing - Main Tank, Rib 5 to Rib 22, Wing Station 204.25 to Wing BL 643.50
631 Right Wing - Center Fuel Tank, Rib 1 to Rib 5
632 Right Wing - Main Tank, Rib 5 to Rib 22, Wing Station 204.25 to Wing Station
643.50
D. Evaluation
NOTE:  developed the following questions that operators can use to do an evaluation for
wing tank lateral fuel imbalances exceeding 1000 lb (454 kg).
SUBTASK 05-51-48-210-001
(1) If the imbalance exceedance occurred during flight (climb/cruise/descent), then the following
questions apply:
(a) Was the amount of imbalance greater than or equal to 3000 lb (1361 kg)?
1) If yes, do this task: Severe or Unusual Turbulence, Excessive Maneuver, Buffet, or
Speeds More than the Design Limits Conditional Inspection,
TASK 05-51-04-210-801.
(b) Was the amount of imbalance greater than 1000 lb (454 kg) but less than 3000 lb
(1361 kg)?
1) If yes, the following questions apply:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
a) Did the airplane encounter any moderate turbulence (gusts) during the
imbalance?
<1> If yes, do this task: Severe or Unusual Turbulence, Excessive
Maneuver, Buffet, or Speeds More than the Design Limits Conditional
Inspection, TASK 05-51-04-210-801.
b) Did the airplane experience significant load factors or perform rapid or large
alternating control inputs during the imbalance?
<1> If yes, do this task: Severe or Unusual Turbulence, Excessive
Maneuver, Buffet, or Speeds More than the Design Limits Conditional
Inspection, TASK 05-51-04-210-801.
SUBTASK 05-51-48-210-002
(2) If the imbalance exceedance occurred during landing, then the following questions apply:
(a) Was the amount of imbalance greater than or equal to 3000 lb (1361 kg)?
1) If yes, do the visual inspection portion of HARD LANDING OR
OVERWEIGHT/HARD LANDING OR HIGH DRAG/SIDE LOAD CONDITION -
MAINTENANCE PRACTICES (CONDITIONAL INSPECTION),
PAGEBLOCK 05-51-01/201.
(b) Was the amount of imbalance greater than 1000 lb (454 kg) but less than 3000 lb
(1361 kg)?
1) If yes, the following questions apply:
a) Was there a large roll angle during landing?
<1> If yes, do the visual inspection portion of HARD LANDING OR
OVERWEIGHT/HARD LANDING OR HIGH DRAG/SIDE LOAD
CONDITION - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES (CONDITIONAL
INSPECTION), PAGEBLOCK 05-51-01/201.
SUBTASK 05-51-48-210-003
(3) If the imbalance exceedance occurred during takeoff, taxi, or towing, then the following
questions apply:
(a) Was the amount of imbalance greater than or equal to 3000 lb (1361 kg)?
1) If yes, do the high drag/side load inspection (HARD LANDING OR
OVERWEIGHT/HARD LANDING OR HIGH DRAG/SIDE LOAD CONDITION -
MAINTENANCE PRACTICES (CONDITIONAL INSPECTION),
PAGEBLOCK 05-51-01/201).
(b) Was the amount of imbalance greater than 1000 lb (454 kg) but less than 3000 lb
(1361 kg)?
1) If yes, the following questions apply:
a) Was noticeable runway roughness encountered during takeoff, taxi, or towing?
<1> If yes, do the high drag/side load inspection (HARD LANDING OR
OVERWEIGHT/HARD LANDING OR HIGH DRAG/SIDE LOAD
CONDITION - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES (CONDITIONAL
INSPECTION), PAGEBLOCK 05-51-01/201).
b) Did the airplane experience a hard ground turn or a significant side load event
during taxi or towing?
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
<1> If yes, do the high drag/side load inspection (HARD LANDING OR
OVERWEIGHT/HARD LANDING OR HIGH DRAG/SIDE LOAD
CONDITION - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES (CONDITIONAL
INSPECTION), PAGEBLOCK 05-51-01/201).
c) Was hard braking applied during taxi or towing?
<1> If yes, do the high drag/side load inspection (HARD LANDING OR
OVERWEIGHT/HARD LANDING OR HIGH DRAG/SIDE LOAD
CONDITION - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES (CONDITIONAL
INSPECTION), PAGEBLOCK 05-51-01/201).
NOTE: If a lateral imbalance exceedance has persisted for an
unknown number of flights for a particular airplane,
requires that all the inspections noted above be performed.
This is due to the increased probability that the aircraft would
have experienced loads above those typically encountered in
normal operation.
NOTE: If none of the inspections above are applicable to the particular
event, the airplane may return to revenue service. If inspections
are determined necessary based on the operator’s answers to
the questions above, all inspections must be performed before
the airplane may return to revenue service.

ATA 05-51-51

05-51-51-200-801Extreme High Wind Event - Conditional InspectionPDF p. 1057
1. Extreme High Wind Event - Conditional Inspection
A. General
(1) This procedure has information for an aircraft that has had an extreme high wind event while
parked or moored.
(a) Extreme high wind events are tornadoes and microbursts, or when wind speeds exceed
75 mph (65 knots).
(b) Evidence of an extreme high wind event are if the airplane moved over the chocks or if
there are tire skid marks on the ground where the airplane was parked. This may indicate
that the airplane has moved from the position in which it was originally parked.
1) If the airplane has moved over wheel chocks, it can cause damage to the tires,
wheels, and landing gear.
(2) Extreme high wind events are variable and unpredictable.
(3) Extreme high winds from the side and aft direction while parked can cause damage to the
aircraft flight control surfaces and flight control mechanisms internal to the wings, horizontal
stabilizer, and vertical stabilizer. It is possible that this damage will not be seen during a
walk-around or during pre-flight checks. The integrity of the flight controls is very important to
the safe flight of the airplane.
(4) When the conditional inspection tells you to “examine” a component, look for these damage
conditions:
• Cracks
• Twisted parts (distortion)
• Misalignment
• Wrinkles
• Buckles
• Pulled apart structure
• Loose paint (paint flakes)
• Loose fasteners
• Fasteners that have pulled out or are missing
• Fastener holes that become larger or longer
• Delaminations
• Interference
• Other signs of damage
(5) When the conditional inspection tells you to do a “detailed visual inspection” of a component,
look for these damage conditions:
• Cracks
• Deformation
• Loose components
• Sheared components
• Bent components
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
• Missing attachments
• Distortion
(6)  recommends that operators give  the results of this procedure (if you find
damage or if you do not find damage).
NOTE:  recommends that when the operator gives  their results they title the
message “Extreme High Wind Event Inspection Results.”
(a)  recommends that the operator give the data that follows when contacting .
1) The results of the inspections listed below for the flight controls, doors, and landing
gear.
2) The results of cycling the flight controls.
3) If the airplane has moved from the location where it was parked.
a) If the airplane moved over the chocks.
<1> If the main landing gear tires or nose landing gear tires have been
replaced.
b) If there are tire skid marks on the ground.
4) Wind characteristics:
a) Wind direction and airplane parking direction (angle between the two
directions)
b) Average wind speed
c) Maximum wind gust speed
d) Type of wind event
5) Gross Weight
6) Center of Gravity (CG)
7) Airplane Restraints
a) chocks
b) mooring configuration
c) brakes
8) Surface Conditions
a) icy
b) wet
c) dry
d) clean
e) dirty/sandy
f) ground friction test
9) Ambient Air Temperature (C°) at time of event
