SUBTASK 05-55-45-420-002
(1) Do the Joint Resistance check for connectors listed in Table 611:
(a) For W1268-D30408:
1) Place the LRT Sense coupler on W1268 common to connector D30408.
2) Place the LRT Drive coupler on W1272 common to connector D30402.
3) Placing one Joint probe on D30408's receptacle and the other on the strut tray
primary structure, measure the joint resistance and record the value on the data
sheet (TASK 05-56-04-200-801 or TASK 05-56-05-200-801).
(b) For W1268-D30410:
1) Place the LRT Sense coupler on W1268 common to connector D30410.
2) Place the LRT Drive coupler on W1272 common to connector D30406.
3) Placing one Joint probe on D30410's receptacle and the other on the strut tray
primary structure, measure the joint resistance and record the value on the data
sheet (TASK 05-56-04-200-801 or TASK 05-56-05-200-801).
(c) For W1272-D30402:
1) Place the LRT Sense coupler on W1272 common to connector D30402.
2) Place the LRT Drive coupler on W1268 common to connector D30408.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
3) Placing one Joint probe on D30402's receptacle and the other on the strut tray
primary structure, measure the joint resistance and record the value on the data
sheet (TASK 05-56-04-200-801 or TASK 05-56-05-200-801).
(d) For W1272-D30406:
1) Place the LRT Sense coupler on W1272 common to connector D30406.
2) Place the LRT Drive coupler on W1268 common to connector D30410.
3) Placing one Joint probe on D30406's receptacle and the other on the strut tray
primary structure, measure the joint resistance and record the value on the data
sheet (TASK 05-56-04-200-801 or TASK 05-56-05-200-801).

SUBTASK 05-55-45-200-036
(3) Do the functional check of the wire bundle shielding:
NOTE: This step does the check of the wire bundle shielding for the scheduled maintenance
check. This step also does the check of the wire bundle shielding after any repair is
done with the wire bundle or connector.
(a) Measure the loop resistance for each wire bundle listed in Table 612 using the loop
resistance tester, SPL-1636, or MK loop resistance tester, SPL-18565, correspondingly
(TASK 05-56-03-200-801 or TASK 05-56-05-200-801).
NOTE: In the case of multiple wire bundles going to/from a connector, make sure that
the coupler is only around the desired bundle. This can require removing (and
replacing) wire ties to separate the bundles enough for coupler connection.
1) Record the measured value to the data sheet.
2) Make sure that the measured value is within the MIN/MAX value range listed in the
data sheet.
3) If the measured value is not within the MIN/MAX value range, do the
troubleshooting step below for the wire bundle shielding failure.
4) This step is complete when all wire bundles listed in Table 612 were tested and
passed.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 05-55-45-810-007
(4) If it is necessary, do the troubleshooting for the wire bundle shielding:
NOTE: Do this step only if the measured value of the functional check of the wire bundle
shielding is not within the MIN/MAX value range.
NOTE: Record all the measurement data to the data sheet. This should include both initial and
final values. Also record the troubleshooting steps taken to the RETEST MEASURED
VALUE/COMMENTS column.
(a) If the wire bundle shield resistance is less than the MIN value, do the following:
1) Do the check of the test setup and make sure that the couplers are only around the
desired wire bundle and closed properly.
2) If the test setup is OK, do a check of the operation of the LRT or ExLRT
(TASK 05-56-02-200-801 or TASK 05-56-02-200-802).
3) If no problem is found, do a check of the entire length of the wire bundle for signs of
chafing or damage to the wire bundle that can cause the shield to short to structure.
NOTE: An example could be an area where bundle insulation has degraded and a
portion of the shield is exposed and making contact with structure at an
intermediate point in the bundle length. Another could be some metallic
object penetrating the insulation and making contact between the shield
and structure.
a) If a problem is found, repair or replace (SWPM Chapter 20).
4) If no defects are found with the wire bundle and the loop resistance value stays less
than the MIN value, record this value and contact  for support.
(b) If the wire bundle shield loop resistance is more than the MAX value, do the following:
1) Measure the joint resistance across the connector from the ground terminal to
primary structure (TASK 05-56-04-200-801 or TASK 05-56-05-200-801).
a) If the joint value measured is more than the maximum joint resistance value in
the data table listed in TASK 05-56-04-200-801 or TASK 05-56-05-200-801,
correct the problem (SWPM Chapter 20).
b) If the measured resistance value stays more than the maximum value given in
the data table, do this step:
<1> Record the resistance value and contact  for support.
(c) After the wire bundle or connector is repaired, do the functional check of the wire bundle
shielding again on this wire bundle.

E. Procedure
SUBTASK 05-55-46-280-005
(1) Do this task to test W3399-D1857:
(a) Connect one end of the 12 foot jumper, (jumper cable assembly, LRT (loop resistance
tester), SPL-8965) or (ExLRT jumper cable kit, SPL-18884), to the housing of switch
S773 (NOT the switch connector itself).
(b) Connect the other end of the 12 foot jumper, (jumper cable assembly, LRT (loop
resistance tester), SPL-8965) or (ExLRT jumper cable kit, SPL-18884), to ground terminal
GD479DC.
(c) Attach the drive coupler of the LRT to the 12-foot jumper cable.
(d) Attach the sense coupler of the LRT to the W3399 wire bundle.
(e) Do the Modified Loop Resistance Measurement (TASK 05-56-03-200-801 or
TASK 05-56-05-200-801) for this setup loop. Make sure the loop resistance value is
between 10 - 75 milliohms.
NOTE: The loop resistance value is for reference only (do not record).
(f) Measure the joint resistance (TASK 05-56-04-200-801 or TASK 05-56-05-200-801) from
the S773 housing near D1857 to airplane structure.
NOTE: The joint resistance value measured in this step should be within the resistance
limit specified in Table 603.
1) Record joint measurement value on the data sheet.

data sheet.

SWPM Chapter 20.
(2) Do this task to test other points listed in Table below:
NOTE: Refer to Table 603 for resistance range and resistance test type.
(a) Place the LRT couplers around the ground wire near ground terminal.
(b) Measure the loop resistance (TASK 05-56-03-200-801 or TASK 05-56-05-200-801).
1) Make sure the loop measurement values are within the MIN/MAX values listed on
the data sheet.
NOTE: The loop resistance value is to determine pass/fail (do not record). Joint
resistance measurements are only required for trouble shooting unless
specified.
(c) If necessary, measure the joint resistance (TASK 05-56-04-200-801 or
TASK 05-56-05-200-801) from the ground terminal washer to airplane structure.
1) Record measured joint resistance value on the data sheet.
2) Make sure the joint measurement value is within the MAX value listed on the data
sheet.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
3) If the joint measurement value is not within the MAX value, repair according to

G. Procedure
SUBTASK 05-55-46-200-002
(1) Procedure to do the Functional Check of the wire bundle shielding:
NOTE: This step checks the wire bundle shielding for the scheduled maintenance check. This
step also checks the wire bundle shielding after any repair is done with the wire bundle
or connector.
(a) Measure the loop resistance (TASK 05-56-03-200-801 or TASK 05-56-05-200-801) for
each wire bundle listed in Table(s) using the loop resistance tester, SPL-1636, or MK loop
resistance tester, SPL-18565, correspondingly:
NOTE: In the case of multiple wire bundles going to/from a connector, make sure the
coupler is only around the desired bundle. This may require removing (and
replacing) wire ties to separate the bundles enough for coupler connection.
1) Record the measured value to the data sheet.
2) Make sure the measured value is within the MIN/MAX value range listed in the data
sheet.
3) If the measured value is not within the MIN/MAX value range, do the
Troubleshooting step below for the wire bundle shielding failure.
4) This step is complete when all wire bundles listed in Table were tested and passed.
SUBTASK 05-55-46-810-002
(2) Procedure to do the Troubleshooting step for the wire bundle shielding:
NOTE: Perform this step only if the measured value of the Functional Check of the wire
bundle shielding is not within the MIN/MAX value range.
(a) If the wire bundle shield resistance is less than the MIN value, do the following:
1) Check the test setup. Make sure that the couplers are only around the desired wire
bundle and closed properly.
2) If the test setup is OK, check the operation of the LRT or ExLRT. To check the LRT
or ExLRT operation, do this task: LRT Lid Standard Measurement,
TASK 05-56-02-200-801 or ExLRT Standard Measurement,
TASK 05-56-02-200-802.
3) If no problem is found, check the entire length of the wire bundle. Look for signs of
chafing or damage to the wire bundle that can cause the shield to short to structure.
NOTE: An example might be an area where bundle insulation has degraded and a
portion of the shield is exposed and making contact with structure at an
intermediate point in the bundle length. Another might be some metallic
object penetrating the insulation and making contact between the shield
and structure.
a) If a problem is found, repair or replace in accordance with the (SWPM Chapter
20).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999;  006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020,
043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203,
205-209, 212-220, 223, 224 POST SB 737-33-1146 (Continued)
4) If no defects are found with the wire bundle and the loop resistance value stays less
than the MIN value, record this value and contact  for support.
(b) If the wire bundle shield loop resistance is more than the MAX value, at the tailstrobe light
location, do the following:
1) Measure the joint resistance on the tailstrobe light connector as the following
(TASK 05-56-04-200-801 or TASK 05-56-05-200-801):
a) Make sure that the joint resistance values from the braidsock to plug and plug
to receptacle are not more than the maximum joint resistance values in the
data table listed in TASK 05-56-04-200-801 or TASK 05-56-05-200-801.
b) Make sure that the joint resistance value from receptacle to Line Replaceable
Unit (LRU) is not more than 2.5 milliohms
c) Make sure the joint resistance value from LRU to tailstrobe light housing is not
more than 5.0 milliohms
d) If any joint measurement value is more than the maximum value, repair in
accordance with the SWPM Chapter 20.
e) If all joint measurement value are not more than the maximum joint resistance
values, do the task below.
(c) At the other end connector of the wire bundle, do the following:
1) Measure the joint resistance across the connector from the backshell to primary
structure (TASK 05-56-04-200-801 or TASK 05-56-05-200-801).
a) If any joint value measured is more than the maximum joint resistance value in
the data table listed in TASK 05-56-04-200-801 or TASK 05-56-05-200-801,
repair in accordance with the SWPM Chapter 20.
b) If the measured resistance value stays more than the maximum value given in
the data table, do this step:
<1> Record the resistance value and contact  for support.
(d) After the wire bundle or connector is repaired, do the Functional Check of the wire bundle
shielding again on this wire bundle.
SUBTASK 05-55-46-200-003

c) If the joint resistance value is not more than 8.5 milliohms, move to connector
at the LRRA Transceiver end of same wire bundle.
2) At the LRRA Transceiver end of the wire bundle, do the following:
a) Remove the LRRA Transceiver, do this task: Low Range Radio Altimeter
(LRRA) Receiver/Transmitter (R/T) Removal, TASK 34-33-21-000-801.
b) Using intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550, measure the
resistance from the RA coax connector shell to the case of the LRRA
Transceiver.
<1> If the measured value is greater than 10 milliohms, replace the LRRA
Transceiver.
c) Using an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550, make sure
that the resistance from the LRU mating coax connector shell, in the rack, to
the cable backshell on the other side of the connector block (the cable going to
the antenna) is no greater than 5 milliohms.
<1> If the measured value is greater than 5 milliohms, troubleshoot the joint
and either replace the coax connector block, repair the coax connector
on the antenna cable, or replace the antenna cable connector.
<2> If any repair is done, repeat the bond resistance measurement to verify
that the measured resistance is now 5 milliohms or less.
d) Re-install the LRRA Transceiver, do this task: Low Range Radio Altimeter
(LRRA) Receiver/Transmitter (R/T) Installation, TASK 34-33-21-400-801.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
e) If a measured resistance value stays more than the given maximum value for
the joint, do this step:
<1> Record the resistance value and contact  for support.
(c) After the wire bundle or connector is repaired, do the Functional Check of the wire bundle
shielding again on this wire bundle.

bundle being measured. Look for signs of chafing or damage to the wire bundle that
would result in the shielding shorting to structure somewhere along its length.
NOTE: An example might be an area where bundle insulation has degraded and a
portion of the shield is exposed and making contact with structure at an
intermediate point in the bundle length. Another might be some metallic object
penetrating the insulation and making contact between the shield and structure.

2) If a problem was found and repaired, retest the wire bundle (FQIS Wiring And
Bonding - Inspection, TASK 05-55-54-200-801).

A. References

B. Tools/Equipment

C. Procedure
SUBTASK 05-56-01-760-001
(1) Connect one intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550 probe to one side of a
complex joint build-up (structure, LRU, receptacle, bracket, or connector backshell for
example) within 1 inch of the joint being measured.
NOTE: A joint may have several electrical connections. For example, a connector mounted on
a bracket which is mounted to structure can provide five connections between the
bundle shield and "ground": The shield is (1) connected to the connector backshell
which is (2) connected to the connector itself which (3) connects to the receptacle
which (4) is mounted on the bracket which is (5) connected to structure.
(a) Several kinds of possible measurement connections are shown in (Figure 201).
SUBTASK 05-56-01-760-002
(2) Connect the second joint probe to the other side of the joint being measured, within 1 inch of
the joint/connector.
NOTE: It may be necessary to wiggle the probes in order to make electrical contact through
surface coatings.
SUBTASK 05-56-01-760-003
(3) Record the resistance value of this joint from the Bond Meter display.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) The following resistance values (Table 201) are maximum joint resistance values for
common electrical connections/joints.
Table 201/05-56-01-993-802
TYPE OF JOINT
MAXIMUM
RESISTANCE
(ALUMINUM
CONNECTORS)
(MILLIOHMS)
MAXIMUM RESISTANCE
(STAINLESS
CONNECTORS)
(MILLIOHMS)
BACKSHELL-TO-RECEPTACLE 2.5 5.0
BACKSHELL-TO-PLUG BODY 2.5 5.0
PLUG-TO-RECEPTACLE 5.0 12.5
FEEDTHROUGH-TO-STRUCTURE/SKIN 10.0 N/A
RECEPTACLE-TO-BRACKET 2.5 5.0
BRACKET-TO-BOND STRAP 1.0 1.0
BOND STRAP-TO-STRUCTURE 1.0 1.0
BRACKET-TO-STRUCTURE 1.0 1.0
RIVETED BRACKET-TO-STRUCTURE 1.0 1.0
OTHER FAY SURFACE BONDS 1.0 1.0
(b) To calculate the maximum allowable resistance for a built-up joint, do the following:
1) Determine what type of electrical connections/joints and how many of each are
contained within the built-up joint.
2) Find the maximum allowable resistance for each type of electrical connection/joint
(Table 201) contained within the built-up joint.
3) Sum the individual maximum allowable resistances for each electrical
connection/joint contained within the built-up joint. This sum is the calculated
maximum allowable resistance for the built-up joint.
NOTE: For example, the maximum resistance from a backshell to structure could
be the sum of the following values: Backshell-to-Receptacle +
Receptacle-to-Bracket + Bracket-to-Structure. Adding up the values in
(Table 201) (for an aluminum connector) of 2.5+2.5+1 milliohms each, totals
6 milliohms as a maximum value.
(c) If the measured built-up joint resistance is higher than the calculated maximum allowable
resistance, then do a joint resistance measurement across each individual
connection/joint to isolate the specific high resistance connection/joint.
1) If an individual connection/joint resistance exceeds the maximum allowable
resistance (Table 201) for that type of connection/joint, then repair the faulty
connection/joint.
NOTE: Loose connectors and backshells or pigtails can cause an out of tolerance
resistance reading.
a) If the resistance of the BACKSHELL-TO-RECEPTACLE is not within limits, do
the following task: (SWPM 20-14-11) for connector replacement or repair due
to corrosion or fretting between connectors.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
b) If the resistance of the RECEPTACLE-TO-BRACKET is not within limits, do
the following task: (SWPM Chapter 20) for procedures to repair corrosion
between surfaces.
c) If the resistance of the BRACKET-TO-STRUCTURE is not within limits, do the
following task: (SWPM Chapter 20) for procedures to repair corrosion between
surfaces of a critical bond.
2) After you complete the joint repair, repeat the Joint Buildup Resistance
Measurement to verify the repair.
(d) If the measured joint resistance is less than the calculated maximum allowable resistance
for the built-up joint, then do the Joint Buildup Resistance Measurement on the next joint,
if any, to be tested.
(e) If all of the built-up joints/connections for a particular wire bundle have been measured
and joint resistances are less than the calculated maximum allowable resistance for the
built-up joints, then the Joint Buildup Resistance Measurement Task is complete.

05-56-02-200-801LRT Lid Standard MeasurementPDF p. 1669
2. LRT Lid Standard Measurement
A. General
(1) This task contains the procedure for performing a Lid Standard Measurement with the LRT.
The Lid Standard Measurement is a check of the Loop Resistance Tester (LRT) that should be
performed whenever the LRT does not appear to be operating correctly. Measurement of the
standard resistances on the LRT storage lid provides a quick indication of proper LRT
operation. The Lid Standard Measurement consists of the following two parts:
(a) Loop Mode, that makes a check of the loop resistance measurement function
(b) Joint Mode, that makes a check of the joint resistance measurement function.
B. Tools/Equipment
NOTE: When more than one tool part number is listed under the same "Reference" number, the
tools shown are alternates to each other within the same airplane series. Tool part numbers
that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional.
Reference Description
SPL-1636 Tester - Loop Resistance ( LRT "-1" for checks up to & including 4
years ONLY, LRT "-2 & -3" applicable for all HIRF/FQIS
check/inspection intervals)
Part #: 906-10246-3 Supplier: 3X2T2
Opt Part #: 906-10246-1 Supplier: 3X2T2
Opt Part #: 906-10246-2 Supplier: 3X2T2
C. Procedure
SUBTASK 05-56-02-820-001
(1) Loop Mode
(a) The various components of the loop resistance tester, SPL-1636 are illustrated in
Figure 201.
(b) Open the loop resistance tester, SPL-1636(LRT) assembly and slide the lid aside to
separate it from the base.
(c) Open the lid and remove the Sense/Drive couplers and the Joint Probe assembly.
(d) Connect the blue-coded Sense coupler cable to the blue-coded Sense Coupler connector
on the LRT.
(e) Connect the red-coded Drive coupler cable to the red-coded Drive Coupler connector on
the LRT.
(f) Connect the Joint Probe assembly to the Joint Probe connector on the LRT.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(g) Lift the safety cover and set the RUN-OFF/CHARGE switch to the RUN position.
(h) Set the MODE switch to the LOOP position.
(i) Push and hold the ON/OFF push-button switch on the BITE module until "Testing
Hardware" shows on the BITE display, then release the ON/OFF switch. A four character
symbol will move around the BITE display during the hardware self-test.
NOTE: To conserve the battery, the LRT will automatically power down after 10 minutes
of inactivity. To re-apply power, press the “ON” button.
(j) When the "Press Start" indication shows on the BITE display, make sure the LED on
each Sense/Drive coupler control box is red.
(k) Connect the Sense/Drive couplers to the cutout in the Reference Standard, built into the
storage lid of the LRT.
1) Position the couplers at each end of the cutout, near the Sense/Drive coupler
alignment marks (Figure 201) Sheet 3.
(l) Begin the Lid Standard Test by pushing the START push-button switch on either of the
Sense/Drive coupler control boxes.
(m) Make sure the LED on each of the Sense/Drive coupler control boxes is green.
1) If either LED is red and a "DRV Coup Is Open" or "SNS Coup Is Open" message
shows on the BITE display, then the couplers should be checked for proper
connection.
a) Gently squeeze and release the coupler handles to improve the connection of
the couplers to the Lid Standard. If adjusting the couplers does not change the
LEDs to green, replace the LRT.
b) If "Press Start" shows on the BITE display, then push the START push-button
on either of the Sense/Drive coupler control boxes and begin the Lid Standard
Test again.
2) If either LED is red and a "DRV Coup Is Open" or "SNS Coup Is Open" message
does not show on the BITE display, replace the LRT.
3) If the LED on one or both couplers flashes red, then re-connect the couplers to the
lid after the "Press Start" message shows on the BITE display.
a) Push the START push-button on either of the Sense/Drive coupler control
boxes and begin the Lid Standard Test again.
4) If the message "UNSTABLE" shows on the BITE display and does not clear, set the
MODE switch to the JOINT position.
a) When the message "CONNECT PROBES" shows on the BITE display, set the
MODE switch back to the LOOP position.
b) Push the START push-button on either of the Sense/Drive coupler control
boxes and begin the Lid Standard Test again.
c) If the "UNSTABLE" message continues to show, replace the LRT.
(n) When the Sense/Drive coupler control box LEDs flash green, note the measured
resistance value which shows on the BITE display.
1) Make sure the displayed resistance value is 0.5 - 1.0 milliohm.
2) If the displayed resistance value is not 0.5 - 1.0 milliohm, replace the LRT.
SUBTASK 05-56-02-820-002
(2) Joint Mode
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) With the Sense/Drive couplers still connected to the Lid Reference Standard, change the
MODE switch to the JOINT position.
(b) Make sure the Joint Probe LEDs are red (Figure 201) Sheet 2.
(c) Place the tip of one Joint Probe on the first Joint Probe reference mark on the lid
Reference Standard (Figure 201) Sheet 3.
(d) Place the tip of the other Joint Probe on the second Joint Probe reference mark.
NOTE: The LRT will start the Joint Test when the LEDs on both Joint Probes are green.
(e) When the LED on either Joint Probe flashes green, the measurement shows, in
milliohms, on the bottom line of the BITE display.
NOTE: The loop resistance from the previous loop measurement is displayed on the top
line of the BITE display during a joint mode measurement.
(f) Note the joint resistance value.
(g) Keep the first Joint Probe in place on the first Joint Probe reference mark and move the
second Joint Probe to the next Joint Probe reference mark.
(h) Repeat the above steps until a resistance value has been measured for each Joint Probe
reference mark, 2 through 6.
(i) Compare the measured resistance values with the acceptable resistance values listed
below:
Table 201/05-56-02-993-801
Measurement Points (Referenced to First Joint Probe Mark) Resistance Measurement Acceptable
Values
Second Joint Probe Reference Mark 0.01 - 0.06 milliohms
Third Joint Probe Reference Mark 0.04 - 0.11 milliohms
Fourth Joint Probe Reference Mark 0.07 - 0.16 milliohms
Fifth Joint Probe Reference Mark 0.10 - 0.21 milliohms
Sixth Joint Probe Reference Mark 0.12 - 0.26 milliohms
1) If all five resistance measurements taken above are within the range of Acceptable

2) If any of the five resistance measurements taken above are outside the range of

(j) Change the MODE switch to LOOP.
(k) Disconnect the Sense/Drive couplers from the Lid Reference Standard.
(l) This completes the LRT Lid Standard Measurement.
05-56-02-200-802ExLRT Standard MeasurementPDF p. 1675
3. ExLRT Standard Measurement
(Figure 202)
A. General
(1) This task contains the procedure for performing a Standard Handle Measurement with the
ExLRT. The Standard handle Measurement is a check of the Loop Resistance Tester (ExLRT)
that should be performed whenever the ExLRT does not appear to be operating correctly.
Measurement of the standard resistances on the LRT Handle provides a quick indication of
proper ExLRT operation. The Standard Handle Measurement consists of the following two
parts:
(a) Loop Measurement, that makes a check of the loop resistance measurement function
(b) Joint Measurement, that makes a check of the joint resistance measurement function.
B. Tools/Equipment
NOTE: When more than one tool part number is listed under the same "Reference" number, the
tools shown are alternates to each other within the same airplane series. Tool part numbers
that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional.
Reference Description
SPL-18565 Tester - Loop Resistance, MK
Part #: XLR-9703-01 Supplier: KC432
Part #: XLR-9703-02 Supplier: KC432

SUBTASK 05-56-02-820-003
(1) Prepare the MK loop resistance tester, SPL-18565, for the measurement (Figure 202).
(a) Remove the ExLRT assembly from it's box.
(b) Connect the loop cable [4] to the loop connector [2].
(c) Connect the joint cable [5] to the joint connector [3].
(d) To power on, push the power on button [1] on the rear of the front panel.
NOTE: The LCD display will show the unit information.
1) If the ExLRT does not turn on, do these steps:
a) Open the battery compartment.
b) Remove the battery.
c) Put the charged battery into the unit.
d) Close the battery compartment.
2) If necessary, refer to the ExLRT user’s guide and contact the device manufacturer.
SUBTASK 05-56-02-820-005
(2) Configure the ExLRT, as follows:
(a) Make sure that LCD display shows 'Manual (continuous)'.
1) If it is not displayed, push the select button [9].
2) Use the scroll up button [7] and scroll down button [8] to select 'Continuous
(Default)'.
3) Push the select button [9].
4) Push the stop measurement button [10] to back to Main menu.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
5) Select “Manual (Continuous)”.
6) Push the select button [9].
7) Select “Continuous (Default)”.
8) Push the select button [9].
D. ExLRT Standard Measurement
SUBTASK 05-56-02-820-006
(1) Do the self-test of the ExLRT, as follows:
(a) Clamp the couplers of the loop cable [4] to the self-test handle of ExLRT.
(b) Push the start measurement button [6].
(c) Make sure that the loop status indicator is amber.
(d) Record the value of the Loop resistance.
NOTE: The loop measurements are displayed as a number with two decimal places on
left top of LCD screen.
1) If either the loop status indicator is red and “Drive coupler is open” or “Sense
Coupler is Open” message shows on the LCD display, do these steps:
a) Gently squeeze and release the coupler handles to improve the connection of
the coupler around the wire bundle being measured.
b) If adjusting the couplers does not change the loop status indicator to amber,
use a different set of calibrated loop couplers.
c) If error message disappears and loop status indicator is flashing green, push
the start measurement button [6].
2) If the loop status indicator is red and “Loop Unstable” message shows on the LCD
display, contact the manufacturer.
(e) Attach the one pin of the joint cable [5] on the joint probe reference mark 1 on self-test
handle of ExLRT.
(f) Attach the second pin of the joint cable [5] on the joint probe reference mark 4.
(g) Record the value of the Joint 1 resistance.
NOTE: The joint measurement will be displayed as a number with two decimal places on
right top of LCD screen.
1) If joint status indicator is red, check the LCD display for an error message.
2) If necessary, refer to the ExLRT user’s guide for corrective action based on display
error message.
(h) Attach the one pin of the joint cable [5] on the joint probe reference mark 2.
(i) Attach the second pin of the joint cable [5] on the joint probe reference mark 3.
(j) Record the value of the Joint 2 resistance.
NOTE: The joint measurement will be displayed as a number with two decimal places on
right top of LCD screen.
1) If joint status indicator is red, check the LCD display for an error message.
2) If necessary, refer to the ExLRT user’s guide for corrective action based on display
error message.
SUBTASK 05-56-02-820-007
(2) If unable to complete the joint resistance measurement, do the steps that follows:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) If the joint status indicator is red, check the LCD display for an error message.
1) If the message on the LCD displays "Joint Intermittent", do the following:
a) Push the stop measurement button [10] and remove the joint probes from the
connector to stop the measurement.
b) Push the start measurement button [6] and re-position probes to correct
locations to start measurement.
c) If this fails to clear the "Joint Intermittent" message, contact the manufacturer.
2) If the message on the LCD displays a “Probes not connected to UUT", do the
following:
a) Push the stop measurement button [10] and remove the joint probes from the
connector to stop the measurement.
b) Push the start measurement button [6] and re-position probes to correct
locations to start measurement.
3) If this fails to clear the message, then use a different set of calibrated probes.
4) If another set of calibrated probes isn't available or doesn't resolve the error
message, contact the manufacturer.
SUBTASK 05-56-02-820-008
(3) Compare the measured resistance values with the acceptable resistance values (Table 202).
Table 202/05-56-02-993-802
Measurement Types Resistant Measurement Acceptable value
Loop Resistance 9.0–10.0 Milioms
Joint 1 Resistance 7.5–8.5 Milioms
Joint 2 Resistance 0.1–0.3 Milioms
(a) If either the loop or joint resistance values are not in the acceptable range, contact the

(b) If all resistance measurements are in the acceptable range, then this task is completed

(c) Remove the couplers from the self-test handle of the ExLRT.

D. Loop Resistance Measurement
SUBTASK 05-56-03-760-001
(1) Connect the couplers.
(a) For a normal loop resistance tester, SPL-1636 (Figure 202):
1) Clamp both of the LRT couplers around the wire bundle to be measured.
a) If there are ground wires, such as shield pigtail connections, at the point of
measurement on the measured bundle, make sure that such wiring is NOT
included within either coupler.
b) Make sure that there is at least four inches separation between the two
couplers. If such separation is impossible to maintain, use the Mu-Metal
shields (P/N 906-10249-9) provided with the LRT to obtain the necessary
isolation.
NOTE: In the case of multiple wire bundles going to/from a connector, make
sure the coupler is only around the desired bundle. This may require
removing (and replacing) wire ties to separate the bundles enough for
coupler connection.
(b) For a Modified Loop Resistance Measurement (Figure 203):
1) Clamp the Drive coupler around the ground return jumper cable.
2) Clamp the Sense coupler around the bundle to be tested.
NOTE: A minimum separation of four inches between the couplers should still be
maintained.
a) If there are ground wires, such as shield pigtail connections, at the point of
measurement on the bundle, make sure that such wiring is NOT included
within the Sense coupler.
SUBTASK 05-56-03-760-002
(2) Initiate a Loop Resistance Measurement by pushing the START pushbutton on either of the
Sense/Drive Coupler Control Boxes, causing the LEDs on both boxes to turn green.
(a) When the LEDs flash green, note the loop resistance value shown on the LRT BITE
display.
(b) This completes the Loop Resistance measurement.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 05-56-03-810-001
(3) If you are unable to complete the Loop Resistance Measurement, do the steps that follow:
(a) If either LED is red and a "DRV Coup Is Open" or "SNS Coup Is Open" message shows
on the BITE display, then the couplers should be checked for proper connection.
1) Gently squeeze and release the coupler handles to improve the connection of the
couplers around the wire bundle being measured.
a) If adjusting the couplers does not change the LEDs to green, replace the LRT.
2) If "Press Start" shows on the BITE display, then push the START pushbutton on
either of the Sense/Drive coupler control boxes and begin the Loop Resistance
Measurement again.
(b) If either LED is red and a "DRV Coup Is Open" or "SNS Coup Is Open" message does
not show on the BITE display, replace the LRT.
(c) If the LED on one or both couplers flashes red, then re-connect the couplers to the wire
bundle being measured after the "Press Start" message shows on the BITE display.
1) Push the START pushbutton on either coupler control box and begin the Loop
Resistance Measurement again.
(d) If the message "UNSTABLE" is displayed and does not clear, set the MODE switch to the
JOINT position.
1) When the message "Connect Probes" shows on the BITE display, set the MODE
switch back to the LOOP position.
2) When the "Press Start" message appears, push the Start pushbutton on either of
the coupler control boxes and begin the Loop Resistance Measurement again.
3) If this fails to clear the "UNSTABLE" message, then there is a problem with the wire
bundle being measured or with the LRT.
NOTE: The "UNSTABLE" message is caused by the LRT detecting a varying
resistance. This varying resistance can be caused by a loose connection, a
corroded or intermittent electrical joint, a faulty Transorb adapter, or a faulty
LRT.
a) Make sure that the LRT is operating correctly, do this task: LRT Lid Standard
Measurement, TASK 05-56-02-200-801.
b) If the LRT is operating correctly, then the wire bundle or a connection/joint is
faulty and must be repaired or replaced before continuing the measurement.
<1> Check each electrical connection in the circuit being measured to
isolate the faulty connection/joint, do this task: Joint Resistance
Measurement, TASK 05-56-04-200-801.
(e) If the BITE display shows "Joint V TooBig" (Dash-2 LRT only), "Loop I TooBig" or "Loop V
TooBig", then stray currents may be circulating through the shield of the wire bundle
being measured.
1) If power is applied to any of the equipment attached to this bundle, remove power
from the equipment.
2) Any on-board electrical equipment that does not need to be ON should be turned
OFF.
3) Make sure that no other sources of current or voltage are connected on or near the
bundle being tested.
4) In extreme cases, all power may need to be removed from the airplane.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 05-56-03-810-002
(4) For a Dash-2 or -3 LRT, the following BITE display messages may also appear:
(a) Joint TooSmall:
1) This indication is displayed when the Joint Value is too small compared to the Loop
Value to give an accurate Joint reading. This condition exceeds the operating
capabilities of the LRT.
(b) LNoise V TooBig:
1) This indication is displayed when excessive noise voltage on the wire bundle shield
interferes with the LRTs ability to read accurately during Loop Mode. Stray signals
on the wire shield may be produced by motors, electronic equipment, or adjacent
electronic circuits. This condition can be alleviated by de-energizing equipment in
the vicinity of the circuit being tested.
(c) LNoise I TooBig:
1) This indication is displayed when excessive noise current on the wire bundle shield
interferes with the LRTs ability to read accurately during Loop Mode. Stray signals
on the wire shield may be produced by motors, electronic equipment, or adjacent
electronic circuits. This condition can be alleviated by de-energizing equipment in
the vicinity of the circuit being tested.
(d) JNoise V TooBig:
1) This indication is displayed when excessive noise voltage on the wire bundle shield
interferes with the LRTs ability to read accurately during Joint Mode. Stray signals
on the wire shield may be produced by motors, electronic equipment, or adjacent
electronic circuits. This condition can be alleviated by de-energizing equipment in
the vicinity of the circuit being tested.
(e) JNoise I TooBig:
1) This indication is displayed when excessive noise current on the wire bundle shield
interferes with the LRTs ability to read accurately during Joint Mode. Stray signals
on the wire shield may be produced by motors, electronic equipment, or adjacent
electronic circuits. This condition can be alleviated by de-energizing equipment in
the vicinity of the circuit being tested.

2. Joint Resistance Measurement
A. References
Reference Title

SWPM 20-20-00 ELECTRICAL BONDING PROCESSES

B. Procedure
SUBTASK 05-56-04-760-001
(1) To establish an electrical current flow in the wire bundle, joints/connections and bonding straps
being measured, do this task: Loop Resistance Measurement, TASK 05-56-03-200-801 before
starting the Joint Resistance Measurement.
NOTE: Before a Joint Resistance measurement can be performed, a Loop measurement must
have been completed on the wire bundle associated with the joint being measured. If
this is a modified loop formed with a ground return jumper cable, then the LRT
Sense/Drive couplers must be connected as shown for a modified loop resistance
measurement. The LRT continues to monitor the loop resistance of the wire bundle
while the joint measurement is being made. If the loop resistance changes by too large
an amount, the LEDs on both joint probes will blink red and the message "REDO
LOOP" will appear on the BITE display. This message cannot be erased without
switching the LRT back to the Loop mode and doing a loop resistance measurement
again.
SUBTASK 05-56-04-760-002
(2) Set the Mode Selector switch on the LRT to the Joint position.
SUBTASK 05-56-04-760-003
(3) Make sure the LEDs on both Joint Probes are red.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 05-56-04-760-004
(4) Connect one joint probe to one side of a complex joint build-up (structure, LRU, receptacle,
bracket, or connector backshell for example) within 1 inch of the joint being measured
(Figure 201) or (Figure 202).
NOTE: A joint may have several electrical connections. For example, a connector mounted on
a bracket which is mounted to structure can provide five connections between the
bundle shield and "ground": The shield is (1) connected to the connector backshell
which is (2) connected to the connector itself which (3) connects to the receptacle
which (4) is mounted on the bracket which is (5) connected to structure.
SUBTASK 05-56-04-760-005
(5) Connect the second joint probe to the other side of the joint being measured, within 1 inch of
the joint/connector.
NOTE: The LRT will start the Joint Resistance Measurement when the LEDs on both Joint
Probes are green. The LEDs change from red to green when electrical continuity is
established between the probes. It may be necessary to wiggle the probes in order to
make electrical contact through surface coatings.
(a) If the Joint Probes appear to be making good electrical contact and the Joint Probe LEDs
do not change to green and no error messages are displayed on the LRT, then, do this
task: LRT Lid Standard Measurement, TASK 05-56-02-200-801.
(b) If the BITE display shows "Joint V Too Big", then stray currents may be circulating
through the shield of the wire bundle being measured.
1) If power is applied to any of the equipment attached to this bundle, remove power
from the equipment.
2) Any on-board electrical equipment that does not need to be ON should be turned
OFF.
3) Make sure no other sources of current or voltage are connected on or near the
bundle being tested.
4) In extreme cases, all power may need to be removed from the airplane.
SUBTASK 05-56-04-760-006
(6) When the LEDs on the probes flash green, record the resistance value of this joint from the
bottom line of the BITE display.
(a) The following resistance values (Table 201) are maximum joint resistance values for
common electrical connections/joints.
Table 201/05-56-04-993-801
TYPE OF JOINT
MAXIMUM ALLOWABLE
RESISTANCE (ALUMINUM
CONNECTORS) IN MILLIOHMS
MAXIMUM ALLOWABLE
RESISTANCE (STAINLESS/
STEEL) IN MILLIOHMS
BACKSHELL-TO-RECEPTACLE 2.5 5.0
BACKSHELL-TO-PLUG BODY 2.5 5.0
PLUG-TO-RECEPTACLE 5.0 12.5
RECEPTACLE-TO-BRACKET 2.5 5.0

 ALL
Table 201/05-56-04-993-801 (Continued)
TYPE OF JOINT

CONNECTORS) IN MILLIOHMS
MAXIMUM ALLOWABLE

(b) To calculate the maximum allowable resistance for a built-up joint, do the following:
1) Determine what type of electrical connections/joints and how many of each are
contained within the built-up joint.
2) Find the maximum allowable resistance for each type of electrical connection/joint
(Table 201) contained within the built-up joint.
3) Sum the individual maximum allowable resistances for each electrical
connection/joint contained within the built-up joint. This sum is the calculated
maximum allowable resistance for the built-up joint.
(c) If the measured built-up joint resistance is higher than the calculated maximum allowable
resistance, then do a joint resistance measurement across each individual
connection/joint to isolate the specific high resistance connection/joint.
1) If an individual connection/joint resistance exceeds the maximum allowable
resistance (Table 201) for that type of connection/joint, then repair the faulty
connection/joint.
NOTE: Loose connectors and backshells or pigtails can cause an out of tolerance
resistance reading.
a) Do the following task: (SWPM 20-20-00) or (SWPM 20-25-11).
2) After you complete the joint repair, repeat the Joint Buildup Resistance
Measurement to verify the repair.
(d) If the measured joint resistance is less than the calculated maximum allowable resistance
for the built-up joint, then do the Joint Buildup Resistance Measurement on the next joint
in the wire bundle.
(e) If all of the built-up joints/connections for a particular wire bundle have been measured
and joint resistances are less than the calculated maximum allowable resistance for the
built-up joints, then the Joint Buildup Resistance Measurement Task is complete.

a) If necessary, skew the couplers 45 degrees.
3) Make sure that the coupler is only around the desired bundle.
a) If necessary, remove (and replace) wire ties to separate the bundles enough
for coupler connection.
4) Push the start measurement button [6] or green button on the loop controller to start
a loop resistance measurement.
NOTE: The loop status indicator will flash green when the unit is ready to take a
loop resistance measurement.
5) When the loop status indicator is amber, the loop resistance measurement is
displayed as a number with two decimal places on top left of LCD display.
SUBTASK 05-56-05-760-002
(2) For a modified loop resistance measurement (Figure 203):
(a) Connect the ground return test cable to an electrically conductive point of the Line
Replaceable Unit (LRU).
(b) Attach the other end to a grounding point that connects to airplane structure.
(c) Clamp the drive coupler around the ground return jumper cable.
(d) Clamp the sense coupler around the bundle.
1) Make sure that ground wires, such as shield pigtail connections, at the point of
measurement on the measured bundle are not included within either coupler.
2) Make sure that there is minimum 4 in. (102 mm) separation between the two
couplers.
a) If necessary, skew the couplers 45 degrees.
3) Make sure that the coupler is only around the desired bundle.
a) If necessary, remove (and replace) wire ties to separate the bundles enough
for coupler connection.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 05-56-05-810-001
(3) If either the loop status indicator is red and “Drive coupler is open” or “Sense Coupler is Open”
message shows on the LCD display, do these steps:
(a) Gently squeeze and release the coupler handles to improve the connection of the coupler
around the wire bundle being measured.
(b) If adjusting the couplers does not change the loop status indicator to amber, do this task:
ExLRT Standard Measurement, TASK 05-56-02-200-802.
(c) If error message disappears and loop status indicator is flashing green, push the start
measurement button [6] to begin loop resistance measurement again.
SUBTASK 05-56-05-810-002
(4) If the loop status indicator is red, do these steps:
(a) Push the stop measurement button [10] to stop the measurement.
(b) Re-connect the couplers to the wire bundle.
(c) Push the start measurement button [6] to start new measurement.
SUBTASK 05-56-05-810-003
(5) If the loop status indicator is red and a “Loop Unstable” message shows on the LCD display,
do these steps:
(a) Push the stop measurement button [10] to stop the measurement.
(b) If performing a modified loop measurement, re-connect the ground return test cable.
(c) Push the start measurement button [6] to start new measurement.
SUBTASK 05-56-05-810-004
(6) If this fails to clear the “Loop Unstable” message, then there is a problem with the wire bundle
being measured or with the ExLRT.
NOTE: The "Loop Unstable" message is caused by the ExLRT detecting a varying resistance.
This varying resistance can be caused by a loose connection, a corroded or
intermittent electrical joint, a faulty transorb adapter, or a faulty ExLRT.
(a) Make sure that the ExLRT is operating correctly (TASK 05-56-02-200-802).
(b) If the ExLRT is operating correctly, then the wire bundle or a connection/joint is faulty and
must be repaired or replaced before continuing the measurement.
1) Check each electrical connection in the circuit being measured to isolate the faulty
connection/joint.
SUBTASK 05-56-05-810-005
(7) If the loop status indicator is red and “Loop Resistance Low” message displays, do these
steps:
(a) Make sure that ground wires, such as shield pigtail connections, at the point of
measurement on the measured bundle are not included within either coupler.
(b) Make sure that there is minimum 4 in. (102 mm) separation between the two couplers.
1) If necessary, skew the couplers 45 degrees.
(c) Make sure that the coupler is only around the desired bundle.
1) If necessary, remove (and replace) wire ties to separate the bundles enough for
coupler connection.
(d) Make sure that the ExLRT is operating correctly (TASK 05-56-02-200-802).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 05-56-05-810-006
(8) If the loop status indicator is red and a "Loop Resistance High" message displays, do these
steps:
(a) Make sure that the placement of couplers are correct on bundles under test.
(b) Make sure that the ExLRT is operating correctly (TASK 05-56-02-200-802).
SUBTASK 05-56-05-810-007
(9) If the ExLRT is operating correctly, then the wire bundle or a connection/joint is faulty.
(a) Repair or replace the wire bundle or a connection/joint before continuing the
measurement.
(b) Check each electrical connection in the circuit being measured to isolate the faulty
connection/joint.
E. Joint Resistance Measurement
SUBTASK 05-56-05-760-003
(1) Complete the loop measurement on the wire bundle associated with the joint being measured.
NOTE: The ExLRT continues to monitor the loop resistance of the wire bundle while the joint
measurement is being made.
NOTE: Keep couplers in the same configuration.
SUBTASK 05-56-05-760-004
(2) Make sure that the joint status indicator is flashing green.
SUBTASK 05-56-05-760-005
(3) Connect one joint probe to one side of a complex joint build-up (structure, LRU, receptacle,
bracket, or connector backshell for example) within 1 in. (25 mm) of the joint being measured
(Figure 204 or Figure 205).
NOTE: A joint may have several electrical connections. For example, a connector mounted on
a bracket that is mounted to structure can provide five connections between the
bundle shield and "ground": The shield is (1) connected to the connector backshell that
is (2) connected to the connector itself that (3) connects to the receptacle that (4) is
mounted on the bracket that is (5) connected to structure.
SUBTASK 05-56-05-760-006
(4) Connect the second joint probe to the other side of the joint being measured, within 1 in.
(25 mm) of the joint/connector.
(a) Make sure that the joint status indicator turn amber.
(b) Make sure that the joint measurement is displayed in the top right of the LCD display.
(c) If necessary, shake the probes to make electrical contact through surface coatings.
(d) If the joint probes appear to be making good electrical contact and the joint probe LED
indicator does not change to amber and no error messages are displayed, do this task:
ExLRT Standard Measurement, TASK 05-56-02-200-802.
(e) If the joint probe LED indicator is red and the LCD display shows "Joint Low vs Loop", do
these steps:
1) Attach one end of the ground return test cable to the shield termination point of the
electrical connector under test.
2) Thread the ground return test cable and wire bundle under test through both loop
couplers.
3) Connect the other end of the ground return test cable to structure.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
4) Push the start measurement button [6] to start a new measurement, the loop
resistance should be much lower than it was previously.
a) If the loop resistance is not lower, check the connection of the ground return
test cable.
5) Connect one joint probe to one side of a complex joint build-up (structure, LRU,
receptacle, bracket, or connector backshell for example) within 1 in. (25 mm) of the
joint being measured (Figure 204 or Figure 205).
6) Connect the second joint probe to the other side of the joint being measured, within
1 in. (25 mm) of the joint/connector.
a) Make sure that the joint status indicator turn amber.
b) Make sure that the joint measurement is displayed in the top right of the LCD
display.
SUBTASK 05-56-05-810-008
(5) If the joint probe LED indicator is red and the LCD display shows “Joint Intermittent”, do these
steps:
(a) Push the stop measurement button [10] and remove joint probes from the connector to
stop the measurement.
(b) Push the start measurement button [6] and re-position probes to correct locations to start
measurement.
(c) If this fails to clear the “Joint Intermittent” message, then there is a problem with the wire
bundle being measured or with the ExLRT.
(d) Make sure that the ExLRT is operating correctly, do this task: ExLRT Standard
Measurement, TASK 05-56-02-200-802.
(e) If the ExLRT is operating correctly, then there is a problem with the connection/joint and it
must be repaired or replaced before continuing the measurement.
SUBTASK 05-56-05-760-007
(6) When the LED is amber, record the resistance value of the joint shown in the top right of the
LCD display.
(a) The following resistance values (Table 201) are maximum joint resistance values for
common electrical connections/joints.

(b) Calculate the maximum allowable resistance for a built-up joint.
1) Determine what type of electrical connections/joints and how many of each are
contained within the built-up joint.
2) Find the maximum allowable resistance for each type of electrical connection/joint
(Table 201) contained within the built-up joint.
3) Sum the individual maximum allowable resistances for each electrical
connection/joint contained within the built-up joint.
NOTE: This sum is the calculated maximum allowable resistance for the built-up
joint.
(c) If the measured built-up joint resistance is higher than the calculated maximum allowable
resistance, then do a joint resistance measurement across each individual
connection/joint to isolate the specific high resistance connection/joint.
1) If an individual connection/joint resistance exceeds the maximum allowable
resistance (Table 201) for that type of connection/joint, then repair the faulty
connection/joint.
NOTE: Loose connectors and backshells or pigtails can cause an out of tolerance
resistance reading.
a) Do the following task: (SWPM 20-20-00) or (SWPM 20-25-11).
2) After you complete the joint repair, repeat the joint buildup resistance measurement
to verify the repair.
(d) If the measured joint resistance is less than the calculated maximum allowable resistance
for the built-up joint, then do the joint buildup resistance measurement on the next joint in
the wire bundle.
(e) If all of the built-up joints/connections for a particular wire bundle have been measured
and joint resistances are less than the calculated maximum allowable resistance for the
built-up joints, then the joint buildup resistance measurement task is complete.
